column3: Records every player's rating from a match into the month ratings. \n `MONTH_RATINGS::record_match_ratings(game, match)`, called by 0x7683a0 for every match of the leagues that have a monthly award. Both sides of the match (+0x190 and +0x190 + 0x625), 20 slots of 0x49 bytes each: except the slot marked 0xfb at +0x1d and, from the 12th slot on, the substitute who did not come on (+0x32 = 0xff), the person (id at +0) below the person count [0xae2364] goes to the month ratings (0x767fa0).

Finds or appends the person's record in the month ratings table, adds the rating and counts one match. \n `MONTH_RATINGS::add_player_rating(slot)`. The table at [this] (count at +4, capacity at +8) has 12-byte records: +0 person, +4 club's league (or −1), +8 sum of the ratings, +0xa matches, +0xb age. It finds the slot's person (+0) or appends it (growing by 300 with malloc 0x944e46 or realloc 0x945667 when full; the league from the person's club +0x39 and that club's +0x57; the age from the person's +0x18) and adds the rating.

Sorts the month ratings by average and returns the best player of a league, with an optional age filter. \n `MONTH_RATINGS::find_best_player(league, age)`, used by the monthly award (0x767150). It sorts the table by average (qsort 0x945333 with 0x768200: those with fewer than 3 matches go to the end) and returns the first record of the league (−1: any) with at least 3 matches (then 2, 1 and 0); with an age (not 0xff), those above it are only counted and the youngest only qualifies after 3 have been counted; with a league, the current league of the person's club (+0x39, +0x57) must also be the requested one. None: 0.

Finds the nth club of a nation in the South American club table, optionally skipping clubs already qualified and clubs with a human manager. \n `ConmebolSeeding::find_nth_unqualified_club_of_nation`; this is not read; the same code as UEFA's 0x9050d0. In the South American club table (12-byte records sorted by nation: +0 the club, +4 the nation id), a binary search (bsearch 0x946464 with 0x905ce0; the key holds only the nation and +8 = 0xff) finds a club of the nation; it steps back to the first club of the nation, then walks to the `n`th (char, 1 = the first) that counts, skipping, on request, those that already have a place (+0x1db ≠ −1) and those with a human manager (0x600a50(club, 0, 1, 0, 0)). The table is sorted by nation and, within it, by division, position and reputation. The last record of the table is never examined by the loop (if the loop reaches it with the count at zero, it is chosen without the tests). Returns the club if it belongs to the nation, otherwise 0.

Builds the CONMEBOL club table: South American and Mexican clubs (national teams excluded), each stripped of its continental place, sorted by nation. \n `collect_conmebol_clubs` (stdcall, ret 4). It allocates 12 bytes per club in the game (0x944e46; out of memory, the box for line 0xbb and returns 0) and stores the pointer in `*out`. For each club with a nation that is not a national team (0x53b900) and is from Mexico ([0x9cf3d0]) or from a South American nation (continent +0x71 equal to the id of [0x9cfa1c]): it removes the continental place (+0x1db = −1) and writes the record (+0 the club, +4 the nation id, +8 the reputation +0x80 / 500, +9 the +0x69 of the division +0x5b, +0xb the +0x5f; without a division −1 and 0x7f; with a division belonging to a competition without +0x11c, the division and the club's +0x5f are zeroed). Within a nation the order is by division, position and reputation [inference: the division +0x69 and club +0x5f fields]. It sorts by nation (qsort 0x945333 with 0x905ce0). Returns the number of clubs (only the low 16 bits count).

The Libertadores calendar: every new game year it builds the CONMEBOL club table and gives out the places. \n `ConmebolSeeding::update_for_new_season`, called by the Libertadores and by the Mercosur. Without `skip` and with the game year ([0xae2c92]) different from +0x6f: it stores the year, builds the club table (0x4c6280; if empty, the box for line 0x9b and it returns without freeing), gives the Libertadores places (0x4c6430) and frees the table.

Constructs a cup knockout stage: the round table copied from the cup's template (dates, draws), the year, the stage, the id and the parent's rules (+0x49, +0x4a), the team list with pot seeds, and the fixture tree. \n `Cup_Stage::Cup_Stage(parent, n, teams, rounds, a5, template, year, stage, b2, id, b3, tree, by_order, a14, seeds)`; SEH frame with no destructor on the normal path. The base (Cup::Cup 0x518640, mov ecx -> thiscall, ret 0); +4 = a5; +0x40 = the year (word); +0x44 = the stage, +0x42 = b2 (bytes); +0x30 = +0x2c = −1; +0x51 = b3; the vtable 0x969468; +0x43 = 1; +0xb1 = +0xab = +0xac = 0; +0x3c = the rounds and +0x3a = the id (words); +0x49 and +0x4a copied from the parent; +0x28 = a14. The round table (0x944e46 of rounds × 0x68 at +0xa3; out of memory, the box for line 0x48) is copied from the template; +0x3e = n and the team list (calloc 0x945501(n, 6) at +0xa7; out of memory, the box for line 0x53): each team gets status (+5) 0 and its pot seed (+4): the one from the `seeds` vector (given by the cup), or, without it, the position in the list if `by_order`, or 0. Finally the fixture tree, built at once: with `tree`, Cup_Stage::map_fixture_tree (0x5241e0, which links the winners and places the seeds in the first round), otherwise Cup::map_fixture_tree (0x518790, which links at random), both thiscall, ret 0 (they draw); if negative, the box for line 0x62 or 0x6a. Returns this.

Destroys a knockout stage: frees the team list, the round table and each round's fixtures, then destroys the base. \n `Cup_Stage::~Cup_Stage()`, the destructor, called by the virtual destructor. Sets the vtable 0x969468; the team list (+0xa7), the round table (+0xa3) and, if there are fixtures (+0xad), each fixture vector of the +0x3c rounds and the vector itself are freed (0x9452ca, cdecl; the pointers are left in place); finally the base (Cup::~Cup 0x518690, mov ecx -> thiscall, ret 0), whose eax it returns.

Creates the Trophy section stage: a knockout (Cup_Stage) with the 56 clubs in list order (North, then South), using the rounds of stage 0 of the cup table, no seeding. \n `EngAutoCup::create_section_stage()`; SEH frame only for the new, no destructor. The section stage (North and South) with the +0x3e clubs of list +0xb2, in order: a vector (0x944e46 of 4 × +0x3e; out of memory, the box for line 0x2e9) holding them; the rounds through method +0x3c (push 0; push &extra; push &rounds; push 0; mov ecx -> thiscall, ret 0x10); the stage (0x944cf1(0xb2); Cup_Stage::Cup_Stage 0x522e00, thiscall, ret 0x3c: the cup, +0x3e (word), the vector, the rounds (word), +4, the table, the year +0x40 (word), 0, 1, the extra (word), +0x51 (byte), 0, 0, 0, no seeds; the words and bytes are pushed with garbage in the upper bits, which the constructor does not read) into [+0xc][0]; the vector and the table are freed (0x9452ca). Without a stage, the box for line 0x300; with it, +0x30 = 0.

Moves the Trophy on by one stage; when the sections end (stage 1) it builds the final between the North and South winners; at the last stage, the error box. \n `EngAutoCup::advance_stage()`, virtual +0x28. At the last stage (+0x30 ≥ +0x2c − 1, signed), the box for line 0x314 and nothing else; otherwise +0x30 goes up by one and, on reaching 1 (the end of the sections), it builds the final (EngAutoCup::create_final_stage 0x56bce0, direct call with the cup's ecx -> thiscall, ret 0).

Builds the Trophy final when the sections end: a single tie (2-team Cup_Stage, stage 1) between the club still alive in the cup list and the one still alive in the section stage, and draws the round at once (home side). \n `EngAutoCup::create_final_stage()`; from the next stage, SEH frame only for the new, no destructor. The Trophy final: a vector of 2 (0x944e46 of 8; out of memory, the box for line 0x337) with the first club of status 1 (the one still alive [inference]) in the cup list (+0xa7) and the first of status 1 in the section stage list ([+0xc][0] +0xa7), both among the first +0x3e (of the cup); the rounds through method +0x3c (push 0; push &extra; push &rounds; push 1; mov ecx -> thiscall, ret 0x10); the stage (0x944cf1(0xb2); Cup_Stage::Cup_Stage 0x522e00, thiscall, ret 0x3c: the cup, 2, the vector, the rounds (word), +4, the table, the year +0x40 (word), 1, 1, the extra (word), 0x14, 0, 0, 0, no seeds) into [+0xc][1]; the round table is freed (0x9452ca). Without a stage, the box for line 0x35a (the vector is left allocated, as in the original). With it, the round draw (Cup::draw_round 0x51c410: push 0; mov ecx, stage -> thiscall, ret 4) and the vector is freed.

Writes the Trophy final ranking into the cup statistics: the highest-reputation club of each half takes 1st and 2nd; the others share one position per round, from the last round to the first. \n `EngAutoCup::rank_teams()`, the virtual for the final ranking (n = 1 up to 2002-06-01). The final position of each club in the cup statistics (+8, Comp_Stats; without them, the box for line 0x3bb). A vector of 2 × +0x3e pointers (0x944e46; out of memory, the box for line 0x3c3): in the first half the clubs of the cup list (+0xa7, 6-byte entries), in the second those of the section stage ([+0xc][0] +0xa7); each half sorted by reputation (+0x80, word), highest first (qsort 0x945333 with 0x4b07d0). The first two (the highest-reputation club of each half): the one with the higher reputation (signed, strictly) is 1st and the other 2nd (Comp_Stats::set_club_final_position 0x4a2540: push position; push club; mov ecx, +8 -> thiscall, ret 8). Then, for each half, from the last round (+0x3c − 1) to the first, as many clubs (the next ones of the half, from the 2nd on) as the round has in +0x1a of the round table (+0xa3, 0x68 bytes per round), with positions 3, 5, 7... (3, then 3 + 2 × those already placed). The original pushes the dword of the position byte with stack garbage in the upper bits; 0x4a2540 only reads the byte. The vector is freed.

Daily Intertoto update: once a season, when the Intertoto ends, its final winners (up to three, in August) enter the UEFA Cup; every day, the cup update. \n `IntertotoCup::update_for_date(today, stage)`, virtual +0x14 of the Intertoto. Once (+0xb2 = 0), when the cup has ended (virtual +0x10 with 0, 1: push 1; push 0; mov ecx, this -> thiscall, ret 8; the low byte): without the UEFA Cup, the box for line 0x29e; with it, each Intertoto team with +5 = 1 (the winners of the finals) goes, in order, into the places from +0x3e − 27 on of the UEFA Cup's table +0xa7 (the last three places; up to three: the club, +4 and +5 zeroed) and into its entry book (+0x14, 6 bytes: the club and status 4 at +4 [inference: entry through the Intertoto]; +0x36 goes up); then the UEFA predicted positions (virtual +0x5c: mov ecx, uefa -> thiscall, ret 0), +0xb2 = 1 and the predicted positions once more (the original re-reads the UEFA Cup). Always, at the end, the cup update (0x51f890: push stage; push today; mov ecx, this -> thiscall, ret 8), whose return value is returned.

Records a club's Intertoto outcome in the staff records: the final winner qualifies for the UEFA Cup, a club going through gets the next round record, a club knocked out leaves European competition. 
 `IntertotoCup::update_staff_records_for_status(club, outcome, _, _, match, _)`, virtual +0x44 of the Intertoto; returns 0. Weight = 0x4bf850(low, high, match round +0x34, rounds +0x3c) (cdecl, 4 pushes; add esp, 0x10). 
 - 1 (won the final): the qualification record (0x86bdd0) for the UEFA Cup (the competition [0xae23d0] + 0x6b × [0x9cf6f0]), stage 0, round 0xa, weight(0x3c, 0x64), and the club moves to the UEFA Cup (+0x1db = [0x9cf6f0]). 
 - 0 (went through a round): if the next round exists (+0x34 + 1 < +0x3c), the qualification record in the Intertoto (+4) with the match's stage +0x32, the +7 of the next round (+0xa3, 0x68 bytes) and the weight round × 99 / (rounds − 1) + 1 (only the low byte is incremented: inc al). 
 - 0xff or 2 (knocked out, or lost the final): the elimination record (0x86c000) in the Intertoto, stage 0, round +0x30 of the match, weight(0x14, 0x50), and the club leaves European competition (+0x1db = −1).

Returns the fixture list for a year, day, slice and key nation, switching the other year block to the requested year or creating it. \n `FIXTURE_MANAGER::get_fixture_list(year, day, slice, type)`; SEH frame with no destructor on the normal path. The list of fixtures of the year, day (word), slice (byte) and key nation (signed byte) in the chain of year blocks. By the block's year (+0x1130): if the other block (+0x112c) is not of that year, it is switched to the year (0x5aa2d0: push year; ecx = the other -> thiscall, ret 4); without the other block, a new block (0x944cf1, 0x1184 bytes; 0x5a9cf0: push 0; push this; push year; ecx = the new one -> thiscall, ret 0xc) goes into +0x112c; out of memory, the box for line 0x681 and 0. The list: [[block + (day·3 + slice)·4] + type·4].

Reads fixtures_<year>.tmp: each 0x4f-byte fixture gets its club, competition and stadium pointers and goes into the list of its day, slice and key nation. \n `FIXTURE_MANAGER::load_fixtures()`. The name `fixtures_<year>.tmp` at +0x1133 (0x944c9f) and, with a year (+0x1130, unsigned) from 1980 on and the file in CM3_TEMP (0x90bde0: push name; push "CM3_TEMP"; add esp, 8 -> cdecl; 0x945b00 fopen with "rb"), the count (dword) and the 0x4f-byte fixtures (0x945bfe fread; on failure, the box for line 0x730 or 0x73e and the file is closed): the club ids (+0xc, +0x10 → +0x1c, +0x20), the competition id (+0 → +0x14, 0x6b bytes in [0xae23d0]) and the stadium id (+4 → +0x18, 0x4e bytes in [0xae23b0], 0 outside [0xae2358]) become pointers (id -1: the game stops, lines 0x74b, 0x751, 0x758), and the fixture goes (0x68d0d0: push 0x4f; push &fixture; ecx = the list -> thiscall, ret 8; on failure, the game stops, 0x785) into the list of the fixture's day (+0x2a), slice (+0x3f) and key nation (0x48dd70: push &fixture; push competition; add esp, 8 -> cdecl). At the end, fclose (0x945a09).

Collects the clashes of a fixture on its day plus an offset: forbidden dates, fixtures of the same club or stadium, national teams and big clubs, and fixtures already played. \n `FIXTURE_MANAGER::collect_day_clashes(fixture, severity, list, nations, n, date, offset)`; SEH frame only for the dates. Used for a fixture's clashes (0x5ad780) on day `date` + offset (0x54c5b0: push 16-bit n; push &local; ecx = date -> thiscall, ret 8). A cup (+0x3a = 1) only on the day itself. On the day itself, the forbidden dates give 19 and return: 25 December (except in the competitions of the nation of [0x9cf36c]), Sunday in those of the nation of [0x9cf3e4] (0x54a3f0: ecx = date -> thiscall), 10 to 20 April in those of [0x9cf31c] (the dates through 0x549f70: 4 pushes -> thiscall); 17 May with a club of nation [0x9cf408] (also with an offset, without returning, if it is the day itself). Then, for each nation in `nations` (except the 0xff ones) and each of the 3 slices, the day list (0x5abf10: ecx = manager; 4 pushes -> thiscall, ret 0x10) with the cursor at the start: each fixture in it (0x68d1b0) that shares a club and slice (+0x40/+0x41) goes in by type; a club in another slice goes in with 0x14 or 1 by +0x3f and by type 1; the same stadium (+0x18) outside the competition of [0x9cf76c], likewise; the national teams of the clubs' nation (0x53b3d0: push; add esp, 4 -> cdecl) and the clubs with reputation above 5000 by the competition rule (+0x60); fixtures of the competition of [0x9cf690] with a club of the league of [0x9cf590] give 19; a fixture already played (+0x43) gives 0x16. Missing club: the box and the game ends (as in the original).

Finds a fixture's clashes: builds the nations to check, creates the clash list and collects the clashes of the surrounding days; returns the severity and the list, or 0 with no clash. \n `FIXTURE_MANAGER::find_fixture_clashes(fixture, severity, two_days)`, used by the calendar (0x5aa680, 0x5ab510, 0x5ae380, 0x5ae9d0); SEH frame for the new list. Without a fixture or without an output: the box (as in the original). It zeroes the output; the nations to check, without repeats: 0 to 6, the fixture's key nation (0x48dd70: 2 pushes; add esp, 8 -> cdecl), those of the two clubs' leagues, the stadium's (0x48df40: push; add esp, 4 -> cdecl), the partners (0x5af5b0: push; add esp, 4 -> cdecl) and, with a home national team (0x53b900), those of the two national teams (0x48dee0: push; add esp, 4 -> cdecl). Key 3 or 5 outside the competition of [0x9cf7bc] turns off the two days before. The new list (new 0xe: 0x944cf1, push; add esp, 4 -> cdecl; 0x68d020: ecx = block -> thiscall; out of memory, the box and 0) and the clashes of each day (0x5adba0: ecx = this; 7 pushes -> thiscall, ret 0x1c) from the fixture's date (0x549ef0: push +0x28; push +0x2a; ecx = local -> thiscall): below type 0x17, the two days before (with the flag) and the day before; the day itself and the day after; again the two days before with the flag. With no clash: the list is destroyed and freed (0x68d040: ecx = list -> thiscall; 0x944c94: push; add esp, 4 -> cdecl), 0x15 in the output if the national team forbids it (0x776fc0: ecx = [0xb74318]; push fixture -> thiscall, ret 4) and 0. Otherwise the severity in the output and the list.

Clears the leg check list at 0xae2a48 and refills it with the 15-byte records of check_fixture_legs.tmp. \n `fix_man_load_fixture_leg_checks()` (cdecl), from the construction of the main calendar (0x5a9cf0, on load and on game creation): empties the leg check list [0xae2a48] (0x68d080: ecx = list -> thiscall) and rebuilds it with the 15-byte records of check_fixture_legs.tmp in the temporary folder (0x90bde0: 2 pushes; add esp, 8 -> cdecl; fopen 0x945b00 "rb", fread 0x945bfe, fclose 0x945a09: cdecl), using the 16-bit count at the start; a short record: the box (line 0x10b9) and whatever was left in the record goes in (0x68d0d0).

Finds a new date for a fixture: within a window by fixture type, it tries weekdays in a fixed order and keeps the first date with no (or tolerable) clash; otherwise 2 days later. \n `FIXTURE_MANAGER::find_new_fixture_date(fixture)`, used by calendar entry (0x5aa680), by same-day clashes (0x5ae380) and by rescheduling (0x5ae9d0); SEH frame only for the dates. Without a fixture: the box (as in the original). If the units digit of the round (+0x30, 0x4b0850: push; add esp, 4 -> cdecl) is 3 or 4, the fixture's 15-byte record goes into the leg check list [0xae2a48] (0x68d0d0). The window by type (+0x3a): 2, up to the date at +0x24/+0x26 (without it, the box and 2 weeks), starting 4 weeks later (if the end is more than 20 weeks away) or 3 days later; 4 and 6, from 3 days to 2 weeks; 5, from 0 to 1 week; 7, 8 and 10, from 3 days before to 1 week; the others, none. In two passes (the second checking the two days before), through the weekdays in the order 2, 1, 5, 6, 0, 3, 4, every 4 days of the window: the target day (0x54a2d0) from 2 days after today and inside the window becomes the date (+0x28, +0x2a) and the time slot (+0x3f, 0x5af2f0); with no clash (0x5ad780), or with severity 1 or below the type, it stays. Not found: 2 days after the fixture's date (or after today, if it has already passed).

Adds a fixture to the calendar: fixes the stage, reschedules late fixtures, moves weekend league fixtures to the home club's preferred day, resolves clashes, handles national team fixtures and neighbours, and puts the fixture in the day list or in the other year's block. \n `FIXTURE_MANAGER::add_fixture(fixture, reset)`, used by the cups, leagues, friendlies and rescheduling (20 callers); SEH frame for the dates and the new manager. `reset` zeroes the count of chained reschedulings (word [0xae2a40]). It fixes the stage (0x5af180: push; add esp, 4 -> cdecl), +0x2e = −1; a fixture whose date has already passed and is not played: new date (0x5ab510). A league fixture of the home club's league (+0x57 or +0x60) with no round (+0x30, +0x32) and no stage (+0x3b), once (bit 0x800 of +0x4d): on Saturday or Sunday, it moves to the home club's preferred day (+0x72: 4, 5 or 6) if there is no clash there. With fewer than 10 chained reschedulings, the clashes (0x5ad780): severity 0x14, the same-day clash (0x5ae380) and 1; a cup or type 9 refused by the competition (+0x64): 0; severity at least the type: 0 if the fixture's national team has a call-up ([0xb74434], 0x7e6f20), otherwise a new date and it goes in again; otherwise it goes in (0x5ab230) and the clashing fixtures leave: the friendlies (0x5c6710/0x5c6570 on [0xae2c74]), type 9 (0x5abc30), the others rescheduled (0x5abc30, 0x5ab510, 0x5aa680) with the news (0x5aac70 on [0xae2a58]). In the block's year (+0x1130): the key nation (0x48dd70), the order (0x5ab3c0), the national team fixtures (0x7e6720 on [0xb74434], 0x76bab0 on [0xb74318]), the neighbours (0x5ae9d0, key 3 or 5); if it did not go in, into the list of the day, slice and key (0x68d0d0). Outside the year, into the other year's block (+0x112c: 0x5aa2d0 for the year, or a new one of 0x1184 bytes, 0x5a9cf0; out of memory, the box and 0).

Switches a fixture block to another year: saves the year's fixtures, moves the other block to the neighbouring year if needed, destroys the 366 days' lists, switches the year and leap flag, creates new lists and loads the new year's fixtures. \n `FIXTURE_MANAGER::set_year(year)`, used by calendar entry (0x5aa680, the other year's block), by saving and removing fixtures and by the friendlies; SEH frame for the new blocks. If the same year (word, +0x1130): returns 1. Otherwise: it writes the year's fixtures (0x5ac060: ecx = block; push 0 -> thiscall; on failure, the box and 0); if the other block (+0x112c) is in the requested year, it moves to the year neighbouring this one's (0x5aa2d0 on it); it destroys and frees the lists of the 366 days × 3 slices × key nations ([0xb64738], signed byte; 0x68d040, 0x944c94); the other block in the requested year, if this is the main one (+0x1183), is destroyed and freed (0x5aa0d0: ecx = block -> thiscall; 0x944c94); the new year, leap flag at +0x1132 (0x54cfe0: push year; add esp, 4 -> cdecl), the new lists (new 0xe: 0x944cf1, push; add esp, 4 -> cdecl; 0x68d020: ecx = block -> thiscall; out of memory, the box and 0) and the loading of the year's fixtures (0x5ac3b0: ecx = block -> thiscall). Returns 1.

Writes the club dates table [0xae2a5c], one word per club ([0xae235c]), into CM3_TEMP\club_dates.tmp. \n `fix_man_save_club_dates()` (cdecl), from the calendar save (FIXTURE_MANAGER::save 0x5ac060, 0x5ac394): without the club dates table ([0xae2a5c]), the "Error" box for line 0x1011 (fix_man.cpp). It writes into CM3_TEMP\club_dates.tmp ("wb") one word per club ([0xae235c] of them, fwrite 0x945ce6); a short write: the box for line 0x101b; then it closes the file. If the file does not open: nothing.

Allocates the club dates table [0xae2a5c] (one word per club) and reads it from CM3_TEMP\club_dates.tmp, or zeroes it without the file. \n `fix_man_load_club_dates()` (cdecl), from the calendar constructor (0x5a9cf0, 0x5a9e38: on a new career and on loading the save). With the table already allocated ([0xae2a5c]), the "Error" box for line 0xfe4. It allocates one word per club (malloc 0x944e46 of 2 × [0xae235c]; out of memory, the box for line 0xfec); reads from CM3_TEMP\club_dates.tmp ("rb", fread 0x945bfe; a short read: the box for line 0xff6) and closes it; without the file (a new career), it zeroes the table.

Writes the leg check list [0xae2a48] into CM3_TEMP\check_fixture_legs.tmp: the count (2 bytes) and the 15-byte items. \n `fix_man_save_fixture_leg_checks()` (cdecl), from the calendar save (0x5ac399): with the leg check list ([0xae2a48], LLIST) empty (the count word zero), nothing. It writes into CM3_TEMP\check_fixture_legs.tmp ("wb") the count (2 bytes) and, from the start of the list (cursor +0xa ← head +2), each 15-byte item (0x68d1b0; a short write: the "Error" box for line 0x10e0, and it carries on); then it closes the file. If the file does not open: nothing.

Resolves a new fixture falling on the same day as another: the one with higher priority stays and the other is moved to a new date, with the rescheduling news. \n `FIXTURE_MANAGER::resolve_same_day_clash(fixture, clashes)`; SEH frame with no destructor on the normal path. The new fixture `fixture` falls on the same day as another, the first of the `clashes` list (cursor +0xa goes back to the start +2 and 0x68d1b0 reads it); without either of them, the box for line 0xde6 and it returns 1. It copies both (0x4f bytes) and finds the target weekday from the date of the list's fixture (+0x2a, +0x28; 0x549ef0, 0x417c10, 0x54a3f0): days 0 and 5 of 0x54a3f0 go to 6, 1 and 3 to 2, 2 to 1, 4 and 6 to 5 (0x54a2d0 gives the date). Each one's priority is its competition's (+0x69 of +0x14), +0x15 (21) with a national team at home (+0x1c, 0x53b900); the list's fixture leaves the day when the new one's priority is higher (or equal, with the new one's home club reputation +0x80 higher) and it has not been played yet (+0x43 = 0xff): it is removed from the calendar (0x5abc30) and the new one goes in (0x5aa680); otherwise the new one leaves. The one that leaves gets the new date; with a clash there (0x5ad780, the list destroyed and freed: 0x68d040, 0x944c94), a fixed fixture (+0x3a = 1) returns 0, otherwise 0x5ab510 finds another date; it goes into the calendar (0x5aa680) with the rescheduling news (0x5aac70, caused by the other one). Returns 1.

Returns the club's first year with fixtures: 2001, or 2002 by bit 0 of its word in [0xae2a5c]. \n `FIXTURE_MANAGER::get_club_first_fixture_year(&id)`; this is not read. The first year with fixtures of club `[id]`: 2001, or 2002 with bit 0 of its word in [0xae2a5c]. Returns `ax` (the screen caller compares 16 bits).

Returns the club's last year with fixtures: its word in [0xae2a5c] without bit 0, or the current year. \n `FIXTURE_MANAGER::get_club_last_fixture_year(&id)`; this is not read. The club's last year with fixtures: its word in [0xae2a5c] without bit 0 (halved); with no year, the current year [0xae2c92]. Returns `ax` (the screen caller keeps 16 bits).

For a non-friendly fixture, moves the clubs' fixtures two days before one day earlier and those two days after one day later, if the new date is free, with the news. \n `FIXTURE_MANAGER::move_nearby_club_fixtures(fixture)`, from adding the fixture (0x5aa680); SEH for the local list and the dates. A fixture of a friendly competition (+0x14, 0x5c6710): nothing. For both clubs (+0x1c, +0x20) of a nation (+0x53) with the flag +0x11c: the club's first fixture two days before (0x5acbe0, side 1), not a friendly and with +0x43 = 0xff, moves to one day before it; the first fixture two days after, not a friendly, moves to one day after it. Only if the new date has no other fixture (0x5ad780): it removes (0x5abc30), adds (0x5aa680, 0) and posts the rescheduled fixture news (0x5aac70, with the fixture as the cause).

Reschedules the club's fixtures from one day before to one day after a national team date: each removed fixture gets a new date, is added back and posts the news with the old date. \n `FIXTURE_MANAGER::reschedule_club_fixtures_near_date(club, date)`, from the national team call-ups (0x777940: a club with more than two players called up); SEH for the local list. The club's fixtures (the id in `*club`) from one day before to one day after the date (0x5acbe0, side 1); each one that leaves the calendar (0x5abc30) gets a new date (0x5ab510), goes back (0x5aa680, 1) and posts the news with the old date (0x5aac70, no cause).

Queues the "fixture moved" news: updates the new date of an existing news item for the same fixture, or queues news 1 with the fixture and the cause or the old date. \n `FIXTURE_MANAGER::queue_fixture_moved_news(fixture, cause, old date)`, from the reschedulings (0x5aa680, 0x5abb10, 0x5ae380, 0x5ae9d0); SEH for the local news. The queue at +0x1128 (created the first time: 0x944cf1 and 0x68d020): if there is already news for the same fixture, it only changes the new date (data 5 and 6); otherwise news 1: the fixture (+0xc, +0x10, +0, +0x32, +0x30, the new date +0x2a/+0x28, +0x40, +0x41) and the cause (the same fields of it in data 7 to 0xd) or, with no cause, −1 and the old date (data 0xc and 0xd); it goes into the queue (0x68d0d0, 0xdf).

Returns the stored copy in the calendar whose 0x4f bytes match the fixture's, or 0 if none. \n `FIXTURE_MANAGER::find_stored_fixture(fixture)`: the copy stored in the calendar whose 0x4f bytes equal the fixture's, in the list of its day, slice and key nation (the year block through the chain; the list cursor goes back to the start and walks). Null fixture or none equal: 0; out of memory for the year block: the box (line 0x7cf) and 0.

Finds (or creates) the fixture's year block and appends a copy of the fixture to its day, slice and key-nation list. \n `FIXTURE_MANAGER::insert_fixture(fixture)`: appends a copy of the fixture's 0x4f bytes (0x68d0d0) to the list of its day, slice and key nation in the year block (through the chain). Out of memory for the block: the box (line 0x3ff); a failed copy: the box (line 0x3eb).

Removes the first item with the same bytes from the fixture's day, slice and key-nation list; returns 1 if removed. \n `FIXTURE_MANAGER::remove_fixture(fixture)`: removes from the list of the fixture's day, slice and key nation (in the year block, through the chain) the first item with the same bytes (0x68d1f0). Returns 1 if removed, 0 if not; out of memory for the block: the box (line 0x5ef) and 0.

Counts (and copies into the list, if given) the calendar fixtures between two dates in the key-nation lists of the club or competition, with type, club side and competition filters. \n `FIXTURE_MANAGER::find_fixtures(day0, year0, day1, year1, club, list, comp, type, side)`: counts (and, with `list`, copies into it) the calendar fixtures between (day0, year0) and (day1, year1) inclusive, day by day (366 per year), in the three slices of each day and in the key-nation lists: the club's (index into [0xae23b4], 0x245 bytes; a national team 0x53b900: nations 0 and 1; otherwise 2..7, the one from 0x48dee0 and the partner 0x5af5b0, without repeats) or only the competition's (0x48dd70). Filters: type (0xfe any), club side (0xff any) and competition (−1 any). Returns the count (word); a failed copy shows the box (line 0x93b) and stops there. Hot (288 thousand calls up to 2002-06-01): no counter.

Copies into the list the fixtures of one day and slice for the requested competition, round and type, and returns how many. \n `FIXTURE_MANAGER::collect_comp_fixtures_on_day(year, day, slice, comp, round, type, list)` (from the leagues' TV postponement and from moving cup rounds to the fixed dates): copies into `list` the fixtures of the day and slice, in the list of the competition's key nation (0x48dd70; −1: nation 0), of the competition (+0; −1 any), of the round (+0x34, word; −1 any) and of the type (+0x42; 0xfe any). Returns how many (word); a failed copy shows the box (line 0x634) and stops there.

Tells whether the competition has a fixture on the date in any of the three calendar slices. \n `fix_man_comp_has_fixture_on_date(date, comp)` (stdcall, ret 8; the `ecx` = [0xae2a58] set by the caller is not used), from the European Championship qualifiers (0x57fd60): 1 if the competition has a fixture (+0 = comp) on the date in any of the three slices of the calendar [0xae2a58], in its key nation's list (0x48dd70). Competition −1 or below: 0; null date: the box (line 0xe89) and 0.

Finds the next (or previous) fixture from a year/day/slice cursor, inclusive, matching the competition, stage and two club filters; writes the cursor back and returns the fixture, or 0. \n `FIXTURE_MANAGER::find_next_fixture(year*, day*, slice*, forward, comp, stage, club_a, club_b, ...)`: the fixture after (or before, `forward` 0) the cursor (year, day, slice), the cursor itself included, that passes the filter (fixture_matches_next_filter: competition +0, stage +0x34 and the two clubs +0xc/+0x10, each -1 = any). The group of lists comes from 0x48dd70 (the competition of table [0xae23d0] + 107 × comp, 0). Forward: slices up to 2, days up to 365 (0x16e exclusive), following years from day 0 (the slice only goes back to 0 when the day turns); backward: slices down to 0, then 2, days down to 0, previous years from day 0x16d. Five years from the cursor's year (forward: signed less than unsigned; backward: signed), 0. Found: it writes the cursor (day, year and the slice as a byte) and returns the fixture. The last 3 arguments are not read. The original passes 0x5abf10 the year, day and slice with the high half of locals that were never written (garbage), but it and what it calls (0x5aa2d0, 0x5a9cf0, 0x54cfe0) only use the word/byte: the port passes zero. Used in the cup draws (Cup.cpp 0x519d90, 0x51a150, 0x522c70). No SEH, no box (0x5abf10's only when out of memory).

Returns 1 when a fixture in the day lists uses the stadium, in the given slice or in slices 0 to 2 (slice -1). \n `FIXTURE_MANAGER::is_stadium_in_use(stadium, day, year, slice)`: 1 if any fixture (+0x18 = the stadium, not null) in the day's lists uses the stadium. The groups: 0 to 7 and the stadium's (0x48df40, byte), the latter skipped if it repeats one of the eight. Slice -1 (byte): slices 0 to 2, otherwise only that one. The slice goes to 0x5abf10 in the low byte of the year argument (the original keeps the loop there: the 3 high bytes are the year's). Null stadium: 0. Used when scheduling friendlies (friendly.cpp 0x5c6f00, 0x5c75a0) and in 0x7e6380, 0x7e6720. No SEH, no locals without a value.

Returns the fixture's time slice (1 weekend, 2 otherwise) by the competition's nation and the weekday. \n `this` is not read. The time slice of a fixture of competition `comp` on day `day` (word): the Netherlands, Ireland, Belgium and France (nation id +0x5d in [0x9cf338], [0x9cf2dc], [0x9cf244], [0x9cf300]) only have 1 on day 6; the others, 1 on days 5 and 6; otherwise 2. Returns only `al`.

With the stadium in a third-world country, gives the visiting clubs the illness risk on the day before the fixture. \n `FIXTURE_MANAGER::add_away_trip_illness_risk(fixture)`; `this` is not used. With the fixture's stadium (+0x18), its city (+0x38) and the city's nation (+0x1f) in a third-world country (+0x7e = 3), each visiting club from another nation (+0x53) — the home club (+0x1c, id +0xc) and the away club (+0x20, id +0x10) — gets the illness risk on the day before the fixture.

Returns the fixture list (0x5abf10 of the manager [0xae2a58]) for the year (+2) and day (+0) of the date, in the given slice and group. \n `get_fixture_list_for_date(date, slice, group)` (stdcall, ret 0xc): the fixture list from 0x5abf10 of the manager [0xae2a58] for the year (+2) and day (+0) of the date. The year argument carries in its high half that of the date pointer (`mov ax, [eax+2]`), which is reproduced; the day argument carries the caller's ecx high half, which 0x5abf10 discards (`and 0xffff`): the port passes zero. Used on match days (set_up_the_day 0x6b3c10, Rust, each list of the day), in the friendlies (0x5cbf3e), in the human manager (0x5fe83a), in the media (0x7776a8) and in 0x7e6498, 0x7e6ac9.

Marks the fixture's year in both clubs' entries of the club dates table (year × 2 + bit, 2001 rule). \n (cdecl) Marks the year (+0x28, word) of fixture `fixture` in the entries of the two clubs (+0xc and +0x10) of the table [0xae2a5c] (words: year × 2 + bit 0). Empty entry: bit 0 is set, or the entry is zeroed in 2001, and the year goes in; otherwise in 2001 bit 0 is cleared and the year goes up if larger. Null table: as in the original (error box).

Creates the La Primera table of 20 clubs; first the clubs of the Spanish lower division move to the generic lower division; prize fund of 250,000 per place; TV pays 5,000,000 to each club. \n `SpaFirst::create_table()`. +0x3e = 20 and the table (malloc 0x944e46 of 0x49c; out of memory: the box with source 0xa82844, line 0x250, and 0). Then the Primera clubs ([0x9cf624]) in database order, each in the next row (League::init_table_row 0x687430: thiscall(league, row, club, 0, 0), ret 0x10), until full (not filled: 0). Full: the prize fund (+0x28 = League::calc_prize_fund 0x682f70 with the share of 250,000), +0xe1 = 1, the TV money of 5,000,000 to each club (0x683010: thiscall(league, value, 0), ret 8) and 1.

Writes the club's current, best and worst possible position into La Primera statistics; places 17 and 18 become 16 for the best and 19 for the worst. \n `SpaFirst::set_club_progress(club, stage, current, best, worst)`, virtual +0x68 (from 0x684cd0 for each table row): in the club's entry in the statistics (Comp_Stats::find_club_entry 0x4a4850: thiscall(+8, club), ret 4) it writes the current position (+0x73), the best possible (+0x74; 17 and 18 become 16) and the worst (+0x75; 17 and 18 become 19): the 17 to 18 band of the Primera does not count as a band of its own [inference: positions 17 to 18 join the neighbouring band above for the best and the one below for the worst].

Creates the MLS play-off with eight clubs: the three division winners, ordered by points, and the five best of the rest; the winners go to the final.

 3) The others: the second, third and fourth of each table (in the order: league, stage 0, stage 1, row by row), nine records sorted by points in the same way (ties with no rule of their own); the five best go to slots 7, 6, 4, 2 and 0 (the best in 7). The play-off pairs: the best winner against the fifth best of the rest, the second winner against the fourth, the third winner against the third, and the best of the rest against the second [inference: the pairs follow the list]. 
 4) The round table through virtual +0x3c (thiscall(this, 2, &rounds, &extra, 0), ret 0x10); the stage (operator new 0x944cf1(0xb2) and the Cup_Stage constructor 0x522e00, thiscall, ret 0x3c: the league, 8, the list, the rounds, +4, the table, the year +0x40, 2, 1, the extra, 0x12, 1, 0, 0 and null seeds; the port passes clean words) into [+0xc][2] and the table freed (free 0x9452ca). Without a stage: the box for line 0x5c4. With it: Cup::set_up_round (0x51c800, thiscall(stage, 0), ret 4). The list is not freed (the stage keeps it; the original leaves it so).

Creates the MLS Cup final: the two play-off winners in a two-club cup stage [inference: a single game]; the winner is the MLS champion. \n `UsaMls::create_final_stage()`, the MLS Cup final, from the next stage; SEH frame only for the new. The first two play-off teams ([+0xc][2], the 6-byte records of +0xa7, in order) with the winner mark (+5 = 1) in a list of 2 (malloc 0x944e46 of 8; out of memory: the box for line 0x5e5 and it returns); the round table through virtual +0x3c (thiscall(this, 3, &rounds, &extra, 0), ret 0x10); the stage (operator new 0x944cf1(0xb2) and the Cup_Stage constructor 0x522e00: the league, 2, the list, the rounds, +4, the table, the year, 3, 1, the extra, 0x14, 0, 0, 0 and null seeds) into [+0xc][3] and the table freed. Creates the MLS table (the first division, code 0x413): the four clubs of the competition with that division code, in database order; succeeds if it found all four. \n `UsaMls::create_table()`: +0x3e = 4; the table (malloc 0x944e46 of 0xec, 4 rows of 0x3b; out of memory: the box for line 0x2fe and 0) at +0xb1; in database order ([0xae23b4], [0xae235c] clubs of 0x245 bytes, i16 counter), while rows are missing, each club of the competition with code 0x413 goes to the next row (League::init_table_row 0x687430: push 0; push 0; push club; push eax with the row in the low byte and the code's garbage above, which it does not read; mov ecx -> thiscall, ret 0x10). Returns 1 if it filled the 4 rows.

Sets the MLS predicted positions: in each division the four clubs are ordered by reputation and get positions 1, 4, 7 and 10, one scale shared by the three divisions. \n `UsaMls::set_predicted_positions()`. Without statistics (+8): the box for line 0x675 and it returns. A vector of 3 × +0x3e clubs (malloc 0x944e46; out of memory: the box for line 0x67d and it returns): those of the league table, those of stage 0 and those of stage 1 (the three divisions, row by row), each block of +0x3e sorted by reputation (qsort 0x945333 with 0x4b07d0, highest first, nulls at the end). The first twelve of the vector get, in each division, positions 1, 4, 7 and 10 (Comp_Stats::set_club_final_position 0x4a2540, thiscall(+8, club, position), ret 8; the order of the twelve calls is the vector's); the vector is freed (free 0x9452ca). [inference] The three divisions are mixed in the prediction: each division's favourite is predicted 1st, the second 4th, the third 7th and the last 10th.

MLS result: each game goes to the overall table and, in the regular season, also to the two conference tables (East and West [inference]), without counting the statistics twice. \n `UsaMls::add_result(match, statistics)` (slot 2): the match goes to the overall table (`League::add_result` 0x685d30) with the match's mark +0x42 set to -1 when below 2; in stage 1 (the regular season), it also goes to the tables of the two conferences (stages 0 and 1, through their slot 2, with mark 0 and 1 and without the statistics block +8, which is saved and restored). Returns 1.

Returns the club's conference in the MLS All-Star game: East (0x413) or West (0x414); clubs outside the MLS, none. \n `usa_mls_get_club_all_star_conference(club)` (cdecl): the club's conference in the All-Star game: 0x413 (East) for New England, MetroStars, Tampa Bay, D.C. United, Columbus and Miami (the keys 0x9d0390, 0x9d0394, 0x9d0388, 0x9d0384, 0x9d03a4, 0x9d0380), 0x414 (West) for Colorado, Dallas, Kansas City, Los Angeles, San Jose and Chicago (0x9d03a8, 0x9d03a0, 0x9d039c, 0x9d0398, 0x9d038c, 0x9d037c); 0 for a club whose league (+0x57) is not the MLS (key 0x9cf590); an MLS club outside the twelve: the "Error" box (as in the original).

Builds the World Cup draw list: the seeds into groups 1..8, the other 24 into drawn groups with a limit; in 2002, the real draw and the nation table with the holder and the hosts. 
 `WorldCup::draw_groups()`, from the draw made on the day (0x92e7f0); no SEH. The draw list: 32 entries of 5 bytes (+0 the id of the national team's club, +4 the group 1..8), zeroed (0x945501(0x20, 5): push 5; push 0x20; add esp, 8 -> cdecl; out of memory, the box for line 0x4b5 and it returns 0). 
 1) The seeds (8 slots of 5 bytes at +0xee: +0 the id, +4 the pot; 0xff = already drawn): slot 0 goes to group 1 and slot 1 (+0xf3) to group 3; groups 2 and 4..8 draw one of slots 2..7 (0x90cfc0(6) + 2), drawing again while the drawn slot has already gone. THIS IS THE LOOP OF THE 27/12/2001 HANG (the game stops without an error; worked around by Alan_v2 by changing the jump at 0x92ea55): if fewer than six of slots 2..7 are still standing (in a career started before 2001, seed_teams 0x92f230 does not seed the 2002 World Cup and the slots stay 0xff), the draw never finds a slot and the loop never ends. The port repeats the loop like the original, with no limit. 
 2) The other 24 (the slots at +0x116, in order) fall into drawn groups (0x90cfc0(8)), each group with at most (k / 8) + 1 teams when the kth goes in (k from 8 to 31): it draws again while the group already has the limit. 
 3) In the 2002 World Cup (+0x40 = 2002), after the draw, the list becomes the real draw (the order of `WORLD_CUP_2002_DRAW`: the id of the main national team's club, 0x53b3d0 push nation; add esp -> cdecl), groups i/4 + 1, and the table of the 32 World Cup nations ([+0x14], 6 bytes: +0 the club, +4 the status) receives the clubs with status 6, France (holder) 2, Korea and Japan (hosts) 1; +0x36 (how many) = 32. 
 Returns the list.

The World Cup draw day: the draw list, group 1 in the World Cup itself with its fixtures and sorted table, the group 2..8 stages, the predicted positions and the bookings reset. \n `WorldCup::run_group_draw()`, from the draw day (0x92f1a0); no SEH. The draw list (0x92e940, mov ecx, this -> thiscall); group 1 in the World Cup's own table (0x92d0f0 push list; mov ecx -> thiscall, ret 4; 0: the box for line 0x46d and end); its fixtures (0x6835c0 mov ecx -> thiscall, ret 0; 0: line 0x473); the sorted table (0x6827d0 push 0; mov ecx -> thiscall, ret 4; 0: line 0x47a). With everything done: +0x45 = 1, the stages of groups 2..8 (0x92d540 push list; push g; mov ecx -> thiscall, ret 8, g from 0 to 6), the list freed (0x9452ca push; add esp -> cdecl), the predicted positions (method +0x5c, 0x92f680) and the bookings reset in the competition's body (0x7e9180 push 0; ecx = [[0xae28f0] + 4 × (char)+0x50] -> thiscall, ret 4). On an error the list is not freed (as in the original).

The World Cup day: the seeding on the seeding date, the draw on its date (no table yet) and the league day. \n `WorldCup::update_for_date(today, full)`, method +0x14 of the World Cup, the World Cup's day from the competitions' day. On the seeding date (+0x18e the day of the year, +0x190 the year relative to +0x40: 15/12 of the previous year, written by 0x92d200) and with `full`, it seeds (0x92f230 mov ecx -> thiscall, ret 0); on the draw date (+0xb6, +0xb8: 27/12 of the previous year), with `full` and no table yet (+0xb1 = 0), the draw (0x92e7f0 mov ecx -> thiscall, ret 0). The World Cup itself becomes group 1: four teams, the allocated table, the group 1 teams of the draw list in the rows and the group draw news. \n `WorldCup::create_group_table(list)`, from the draw (0x92e7f0); no SEH. The World Cup itself becomes group 1: +0x3e (teams) = 4, the table [+0xb1] allocated with 0xec bytes (0x944e46 push; add esp -> cdecl; out of memory, the box for line 0x2b1 and it returns 0); the list entries of group 1 (+4 = 1), in order, go into rows 0..3 (0x687430 push 0; push 0; push club; push row; mov ecx, this -> thiscall, ret 0x10; the row goes in cl and the original leaves garbage in the high bytes of ecx, which 0x687430 does not read: the port passes the clean byte), up to 4 rows or the end of the 32 entries; then the group news (0x684230 mov ecx, this -> thiscall).
