Sorts the 32 nations by reputation, sets each one's predicted position (1, 2, 3, 4, 5, 9, 17, 25 by the stage bands) and makes the World Cup the nation's current competition. \n `WorldCup::set_predicted_positions()`, method +0x5c of the World Cup, from the draw (0x92e7f0). Without statistics (+8): the box for line 0x671 and it returns. Fewer than 32 nations (+0x36): the box for line 0x678 and +0x36 = 32. The clubs of the nation table ([+0x14], 6 bytes) in a vector (0x944e46; out of memory, the box for line 0x680 and it returns), sorted by reputation (qsort 0x945333 with 0x4b07d0: push; add esp, 0x10 -> cdecl), and each one's predicted position in the statistics (0x4a2540 push position; push club; mov ecx, [+8] -> thiscall, ret 8): 1, 2, 3, 4, four 5s, eight 9s, eight 17s and eight 25s (the bands of the final stages); then the current competition of each club's nation (+0x53) becomes the World Cup (0x775220 push [+4]; push nation; mov ecx, [0xb74318] -> thiscall, ret 8) and the vector is freed (0x9452ca).

Creates the three-round schedule of a World Cup group stage (12, 19 and 24 June, moved to the weekday) with the two fixtures of each round; the knockout stays with the original. \n `WorldCup::create_schedule(stage, &rounds, &id, &is_league)`, method +0x3c of the World Cup, from the creation of the rules (0x92d200, stage −1) and from the group stages (0x92d540, 0..6). In the group stages (char < 7): is_league (if requested) = 1, rounds = 3, id = 0x420 + stage; the table of 3 rounds of 0x41 bytes (0x944e46(0xc3); out of memory, the box for line 0xcc and it returns 0), the dates (0x68a160: 12, 19 and 24 June of the World Cup year, moved to weekdays 4, 4 and 2, code 1, value 1), game 2 of each round empty (−1) and the two fixtures of each round of the stage (`WORLD_CUP_GROUP_GAMES`). The knockout (stage 7, with the cup routines) and the stages above: the original. Returns the table.

Adds a qualified nation to the World Cup nation table (status 6), or shows the box when the list is full. \n `WorldCup::add_qualified_team(club)`, from the qualifiers (0x90f4f0, 0x911e10, 0x91538e, 0x9184c0, 0x91e200, 0x920500); no SEH. With the nation list (+0x36) below the maximum (+0x38), slot +0x36 of table [+0x14] (6 bytes) receives status 6 and the club, and +0x36 goes up; when full, the box for line 0x456.

Sets the World Cup seeds (holder, hosts, reputation) and the pots by continent; does nothing for the 2002 World Cup. \n `WorldCup::seed_teams()`, from the World Cup day (0x92f1a0, on the seeding date); no SEH. In the 2002 World Cup (+0x40 = 2002) it returns without doing anything: its draw slots come from the database, which is why a 2002 World Cup created by another path hangs the draw (the 0x92e940 loop, cqf_4). In the others: +0x4b = 0; with fewer than 32 nations (+0x36), the box for line 0x59e and it completes the list with the main national team (0x53b3d0) of each nation ([0xae2350] nations of 0x122 bytes) not yet in it, up to 32; it sorts table [+0x14] (6 bytes) by reputation (qsort 0x945333 with 0x4b07b0); the hosts (0x5fa730 on [0xb5e134]: thiscall, ret 0x14, with the World Cup id [0x9cf79c], the year as a word, the two outputs and 1; output −1 = no host) and the holder (the most recent champion, 0x4afd80 of the competition [0xae23d0] + id × 0x6b) go to slots 1, 2 and 0 (swapping places), and the others are sorted again from the first free one; the first 8 become seeds (pot 0, status 3) and the other 24 go to their continent's pot (+0x53 nation, +0x71 continent: [0x9cfa10] pot 1, [0x9cfa18]/[0x9cfa0c]/[0x9cfa1c] pot 2, [0x9cfa08]/[0x9cfa14] pot 3; without a nation or continent, the box for line 0x61e) with the club id in the slots at +0xee (5 bytes); finally the 24 of the table (from the 9th on) and the slots at +0x116 are sorted by pot (0x92f660).

Clears the person's dispute flag and removes her entry from the dispute list. \n `DISPUTE::remove_dispute(person)`: without a person or without the flag table (+4), or with the person's flag at zero: nothing. Otherwise it zeroes the flag and, with the list (+0), moves the cursor back to the start (+0xa = +2) and searches, among the first `count` (+0, word), the entry with the person's id (0x68d1b0): if found, it removes it (0x68d1f0).

Builds the player's strong-position mask from the position ratings and the sides rated 15; returns only `ax`. \n (cdecl) The mask of the strong positions of player `p` from the position ratings (signed bytes): from 15, going down to 10, the first level at which any rating passes gives the sector bits (+0xf goalkeeper 1, +0x10 sweeper 2, +0x11 centre-back 4, +0x12 defensive midfielder 8 or, without it, +0x14 midfielder 0x20 or +0x13 0x10, +0x15 striker 0x40); the sides (+0x17 0x800, +0x18 0x80, +0x19 0x200) only count with a rating of 15 or more (the original repeats the same test at each level). Returns only `ax` (the callers use 16 bits). Null `p`: as in the original (error box and 0).

Returns the pitch cell (column 0..26, row 0..35) of a position by attack and band. \n (cdecl) The pitch cell (`out[0]` = column 0..26, `out[1]` = row 0..35) of position `mask` (split by 0x5b73a0 into sector and side), with `attack` 0/1 and `band` = low word 0..2 (left, centre, right) and high word 0..3 (the height in the formation). The row comes from the sector (tables of 4 by height; in attack, the full-backs 0x80/0x800 move up 1, or 1/4 in sectors 2 and 4); the column, from the side (tables of 5); then the nudges (of 1 or 5) in the bands and the limits. Arguments out of range: as in the original (error box and 0). Returns 1.

Checks the 11 formation slots for conflicts: 0 if any slot with an open side is also a striker's, midfielder's, defensive or attacking midfielder's; returns only `al`. \n (thiscall) The 11 slots of formation `this` without conflict: returns 0 if any slot with an open side (0x880 in cell +0x12d or +0x14e, see 0x5b2ae0) is also a striker's (0x40, in both), a midfielder's (0x20 in +0x12d and in +0x14e through 0x5b2ae0) or a defensive midfielder's and attacking midfielder's through 0x5b2ae0 (8 and 0x10); otherwise 1. Returns only `al`.

Stores the slot coordinate for the phase and ball zone and picks the general and extra positions closest to the slot's 12 coordinates. \n `Formation::set_slot_coordinate(cell, phase, band, coord)`: writes the coordinate (dword: x 0..0x1a, y 0..0x23) of the cell for the phase and the ball band (+0x164, 11 × 2 × 3 × 4 dwords) and, for each phase, finds the positions of table 0x9cc368 (words up to 0xffff) closest to the cell's 12 coordinates in that phase (|Δx·9/27| + |Δy·12/36| against each position's cell through 0x5b7e60; doubled for positions with bit 2; ties go into the phase's list, up to 11 contiguous at [esp+0x64]). The general position (+0x12d) stays if it is in one of the lists; otherwise it becomes the first of the phase with the smallest distance (0x5b59a0 redoes the mask, the cell gets the flag +0x143 and the other cells with the same position lose it). The extra position (+0x14e) comes from the other phase's list: the same position, or one with the same side (0x5b73a0), or the first, or, with two, the middle of the two's bits. Zeroes +0x187f. Arguments out of range: as in the original (box and 0). Returns 1.

Finds another slot with the same general position and sets the output when its flag is lower. \n `Formation::check_duplicate_position(cell, *out)`: zeroes the output; the first other cell with the same general position (+0x12d) decides: with a flag (+0x143, signed byte) lower than the cell's, output 1 and returns 1; otherwise returns 0. With no duplicate, 1. Cell outside 0..10: as in the original (box and 0).

Sets one marking type of the slot (bits 0..2 or 3..4 of byte +0x5b4) and clears +0x187f. \n `Formation::set_marking_type(cell, marking)`: markings 1, 2 and 4 replace bits 0..2 of the cell's byte +0x5b4; 8 and 0x10, bits 3..4; it zeroes +0x187f and returns 1. Any other marking: as in the original (box and 0). The cell is not checked.

Expands each formation slot's positions into the pitch cell tables and their mirrored copy. \n (thiscall) The formation's cell map. For each of the 22 lines k (11 cells × 2 phases) and 3 × 4 block (a18, a14) with the position (i = 12k + 4·a18 + a14) at +0x164 (column, word) and +0x166 (row), the 3 × 3 cells of the block get the column × 9 / 27 in the low nibble and the row × 12 / 36 in the high nibble of table +0x5eb (12 per row, 9 rows per k); the mirror at +0xf9e (row and column inverted) receives (0xb0 − row × 16) with (0xf8 − column) & 0xf. Returns 1.

Returns the stored cell of the slot by attack and band. \n The stored cell of slot `slot` 0..10 with `attack` 0/1 and `band` (low word 0..2, high word 0..3): the dword +0x164 + 4×(high + 4×(low + 3×(attack + 2×slot))) goes to `*out`. Returns 1. Out of range: as in the original (error box).

Sets a formation flag in +0x584, clearing the others of the same group, and zeroes +0x187f. \n Sets flag `m` in +0x584, first clearing those of the same group (1/2/4/8; 0x10/0x20/0x40; 0x80/0x100; 0x200/0x400; 0x800/0x1000; 0x2000/0x4000; 0x8000/0x10000/0x20000) and zeroes +0x187f. Returns 1. Flag outside the groups: as in the original (error box).

Reads a formation from a .pct file, fixes the instructions of old versions, redoes the positions of the 11 slots from the coordinates and builds the coordinate map. \n `Formation::load_from_disk(path, quiet, obfuscated)`, from the creation of the tactics (0x893dc0: the AI formations and the predefined ones, 45 in a career) and from the tactics screens. Null path (line 0x8d8) or a file that does not open (0x8e0): 0 (without `quiet`, the box). It reads the identifier (4 bytes; byte-swapped if the file's marker 0x90c140 is not the native one; minus 123456789 if obfuscated): outside 0x98ec54..0x98ec5e "not a formation" (0x8f7), below 0x98ec59 "old version" (0x900). Then, in order: the password (+0x33, 50 bytes, each byte inverted, 0xff stays), the creator (+0x65, 200), the mask (+0x187b, from 0x98ec5a; before that 0), the 11 general positions (+0x12d, words) and the mask redone (0x5b59a0), the display order (+0x143, 11 bytes, from 0x98ec5c; before that zeros), the 11 extra positions (+0x14e), the cells (+0x164, 0x420 bytes = 0x210 words), in versions 0x98ec59/0x98ec5a 0x108 bytes discarded, the team instructions (+0x584, dword), the player instructions (below 0x98ec5e 11 dwords, each with 10 alongside, at +0x188b every 8; after that 0x58 bytes at +0x188b) and the marking types (+0x5b4, 11 bytes); the last three, if they fail, only show the box. The team instructions get 0x2000 (without 0x4000) and, below 0x98ec5d, 0x20000. The 11 slots redo their positions from the stored cell (0x5b3c70 and 0x5b3560 with phase 0 and band 0); the name (+0) is the file's (_splitpath 0x944cff); the cell map (0x5b7160); +0x187f = 1, +0x1883 = password not empty, +0x1887 = 1. Closes and returns 1. Non-native files swap the byte order (0x43f2d0 words, 0x43f300 dwords, 0x43f350 qwords).

Checks the centre-backs for conflicts: 0 if any slot with an open side is a centre-back's or defensive midfielder's; returns only `al`. \n (thiscall) Like 0x5b8960, for the centre-backs: returns 0 if any of the 11 slots with an open side (0x880) is a centre-back's (4, in cell +0x12d or +0x14e) or a defensive midfielder's (8 in +0x12d; in +0x14e through 0x5b2ae0); otherwise 1. Returns only `al`.

Stores the general or extra position of the slot, the flags, and recomputes the pitch cells without and with the ball (0x5b7e60). \n `Formation::set_slot_position(cell, position, extra)`: without `extra`, the cell's general position (+0x12d, words) changes to `position` (if it changes: the mask 0x5b59a0, the cell's flag +0x143 = 1 and that of the other cells with the same position = 0); with or without it, the extra position (+0x14e) = `position`. Then, for each band 0..2 and height 0..3 (the low and high word of 0x5b7e60's argument), the pitch cells without and with the ball (+0x164 and +0x194 + 4 × (height + 4 × band + 24 × cell)): with general = extra, both from the general one; otherwise, by sectors (0x5b73a0): an extra in a sector below the general's gives the extra without the ball and the general with the ball; otherwise the reverse. Finally +0x187f = 0. Returns 1. Cell outside 0..10: as in the original ("Error" box and 0).

Posts the news of a player's return to light or full training; with a type 12 category, also resolves the outcome of the treatment, the return and the holidays (contract grievances, happiness, liking for the manager, chance of going absent and personality attribute changes). \n `Injury::post_recovery_news(player, stage, type, force, days)`, from the returns to training (0x62e010) and from the end of the injury (0x62e700); SEH frame for the local news. Without a player: nothing; without `force`, only for a club with a human manager (0x7875e0). News 2001 (0x77bbe0) with the stage, the type, the id, the three names, the birth date, the year and the days (0x785790, data 0..8). Category type 12 (the table of 13-byte entries at 0x9e7ad9): random(32000) and: type 'Q' (holidays): with a contract (0x4cf5a0), player sheet and club, each contract grievance (+0x45: 0x20000, 0x20, 0x40) drops (0x8674e0) with random(+0x5b) > random(25); if none drops, random(+0x5b) 0 leads to the chance of going absent (with the absences manager [0xad9c6c] and +0x59 below 12, random(+0x59) < random(5): the absence 0x419840 with 4 and the news is not posted); otherwise the contract happiness (+0x44) rises 15 (−100..100) and, with a dropped flag, the manager likes him more (outcome 2); then random(+0x5b + +0x59, − 5 with player sheet value +0xb above 7250) < random(20) and random(4) adjusts +0x57, +0x5d, +0x44 of the player sheet and +0x59. Stage 0, type 'M' (treatment): 0 gives outcome 2 (form +0x12 = 0xff, +0x13 = 0); below 5, outcome 1 (+0x13 = 0); otherwise outcome 0 and, with +0x5d below 5, the manager may lose sympathy (0x547810/0x547c10, random(+0x5d) 0: rejected 0x547af0); +0x59 (or +0x57) above 10: the manager likes him more. Stage 1, types 'O' and 'N': the outcome by the random draw, the form, and the flag +0xc of the 79-byte record ([0xae2d0c]) is cleared. Data 9 (outcome) and 10; delivery by the reach `force` (0x786090: the club, the nation of the club or of the person, and her continent).

Returns the translated injury category name and the name's gender in language 3. \n `injury_get_category_name(category, text, size)` (stdcall, ret 0xc): the translated name (0x66f4e0) of injury category 0..12 (internal, foot, shin, knee, thigh, groin, upper body, hand, arm, shoulder, neck, head, rehabilitation); otherwise the box (line 0x10e7). Returns 2 with language 3 (0x66f4d0), otherwise 0 (the name's gender). Size below 20: the box (line 0x10d0) and al zeroed.

Records an injury: replaces the previous one only for some types, finds or grows the slot, and records the match, the length, the return to training, the date, the news, the recurrence, the national team, the relapse, the retirement and the outbreak. \n `Injury::add_injury(type, retroactive, person, match, outbreak, news arg, recurrence, recurrence_only)`, from the injuries day (0x62b7b0), the physical effects of the match (0x62c080), the initial records (0x62cf70), the relapse (0x62e500), the illness outbreaks (0x62e9e0) and two original routines; frame of 0x220 bytes without SEH. Null person, no player sheet (+0x61) or type outside 0..0x51: as in the original (box and −1); id beyond [0xae2364]: −1. The day's fitness (0x62c680) and the training ([0xde1f44], 0x8b1750 with 0). Recurrence only: with a recurrence and a type that can recur, the record's relapse flag (+0x12 type, +0x13: 1 if random(rec / 10) and random(rec) both give zero with a negative rec; rec if positive); −1. Otherwise, with an injury (+0xe ≠ −1): only types 0x4d, 0x4e, 0x4f and 0x51 replace it (the remaining days +0x2c are kept, the old one goes to the history 0x58e340 and the slot is freed). +0x1d = type; the first free slot (byte 0xff) of the vector [this+4] (count [this+8]) or 100 more slots (realloc; out of memory, the box for line 0x909 and −1). The type in the slot; the match (through the home club +0x1c or the away club +0x20 that has the person among the 50 of the squad +0xd7) writes the match record at +1 (0x7e4750), otherwise +0x1a = 0xff. The club's best physio (0x544410 of the three +0x1cf with +0x69). Days = base + variable × (35 − best) / 20 (minus a random draw of them if random(best + 5) > random(20); 0 for type 0x51) + the remaining days of the old one (+ random draws by age and by proneness +0x2d of the player sheet, with base above 10). The +0xa of the 79-byte record goes up 1 for each zero of random(5 × natural + 12), per day, up to 100. A current injury (retroactive 0): of 100 days, outside the human club and outside the list, the club's flag 100 in the watch list; days ≥ random(50) + 30, the clubs targeting the player suspend it (0x842b00). +0x28 = +0x2c = days, +0x2a = +0x2e = the return to training (the type's percentage, at most 60 days before the end); +0x20 = the date (today, or today − random(days) − 1 when retroactive). The fitness again, the news (0x62dca0), +0xe = the slot, the recurrence, the national team (0x775cd0), +0x1c = 0, the relapse (0x62e500), the relapse count (from two: retirement 0x7a7f20 by random draw), the retirement by age and by a long return to training, and the outbreak (0x62e820) for types 0, 1 and 2. Returns the slot.

Posts injury news 2000 (the person, type, date, days, birth date and match): over 100 days, to everyone if the potential is above 8000, otherwise to the interested clubs; up to 100, to the human club, the contract club and the national team. \n `injury_post_injury_news(person, injury, arg)`. The function map gives it as stdcall: the original replaces ecx with [0xde1f54] right at entry; the only call site, in 0x62d250, puts the Injury in ecx: thiscall with this unused; ret 0xc; SEH frame without destructor. The interested clubs (0x8d1da0 on [0xde1f54] with 0x5a, up to 30) and the national team (+0x24) if it fits; news 0x7d0 (local): 0..3 the person (id and the +0x33 of +4/+8/+0xc, 0 if missing), 4 = the type, 5/6 = the injury date (+0x20 signed, +0x22 unsigned), 7 = the days (+0x28), 8/9 = the birth date (+0x10, +0x12), 0xa..0xc = the match record (+0x12, +0x16, +9) or −1 with no match (+0x1a = 0xff), 0xd = arg, 0xe = the club id or −1, 0xf = 0x420e9; the match in the news (0x7e4de0 with byte 0x10). Over 100 days: with potential (+0xd of the player sheet) above 8000, to everyone (0x786780); otherwise to the interested clubs (0x7861e0). Up to 100: a human club (0x7875e0), to the club; the contract club (0x4cf5a0) if it is a different one; the national team.

Daily injury update: frees the match knock list, lowers the injury counters, on day 180 of the first season updates everyone's fitness, draws the training injuries on weekdays, then posts the return news and spreads the outbreaks. \n `Injury::daily_update()`, from the day loop (0x5cccd0) and from advancing to the start date (0x5cc850), every day: frees the match knock list (+0x28, 0x68d040 and free); the two counters (+0x2c, +0x2e) of each injury in the table (0x30 bytes at [+4], count +8) go down by one; on day 180 of the first season (0x456770 with the start date), everyone's fitness (0x62c680). Except on Saturday and Sunday (0x54a3f0: 5 and 6), the training injuries: [0xae2364] / 150 random draws (at least 10) of a person: a player (+0x61) — otherwise the draw does not count — in jobs 11, 13 and 15, present (0x418f60), uninjured (+0xe = −1), passing the risk draws (the player sheet's +0x2d, the proneness +0x1e and the recurrence +0x12/+0x13 of the 31-byte record; rating 20: random(5) against random(2)), one in three and proneness of 20: the category (the recurrence's, or drawn by the bands 0x9e7f05/0x9e7f06), the type (0x62d140, serious in the first 1/14 of the draws), the attributes the injury wears (+0x1b, +0x36, +0x1d of the player sheet) and the new injury (0x62d250); outside the season (0x62ce30) nothing; category 7 with a rating below 15 does not count. At the end the return news (0x62e010) and the illness outbreaks (0x62e9e0).

At the human managers' clubs, posts the light training return news and updates the daily fitness of injured players; then processes the return queue: entries due today get the news and past entries leave the front. \n `Injury::post_due_recovery_news()`, from the injuries day (0x62b7b0), every day; SEH frame only for the local dates. At the clubs of the 16 human managers (the last 16 persons of [0xae23bc]), each squad player (50 slots +0xd7) who is injured (+0xe): on the day when start (+0x20) + days out (+0x2a, more than 5) is reached, the light training return news (0x630ee0, once: +0x1c of the 31-byte record) and the day's fitness (0x62c680). Then the return queue ([+0x10], 22 bytes: +0 date A, +8 date B, +0x10 id, +0x14 and +0x15 what the news carries, count +0x18): those with date A today (bsearch 0x946464 with 0x778e90, stepping back while not before today, 0x456740) give the news with the days between B and A (0x54cc30); those with date B today (bsearch with 0x632040) the full return news; those with date B already past leave the front of the queue.

Applies a match's physical effects: for the 20 slots of each side, the recovery at a rate based on the slot's level and condition; the person's knocks in the match list become injuries. \n `Injury::apply_match_effects(game, match)`, from close_day_match (0x6b5f00) and from the simulated statistics (0x84be20), for every match: for both sides of the match (0x625 bytes from +0x1c0), the 20 slots of 0x49 bytes with a person (id at −0x30). The rate: the level (+0x5a in the first eleven with the match flag +0x4c; otherwise the slot's, minus +2 for the substitutes, which with 0xff gives 0) plus (10000 − condition +6) / 100, in 32 bits (the level enters only in the low 16). A game without the flag +0x40: half (16 bits). With it: above 33 + random(3) years (+0x18), × 1.25 (0x968928, _ftol); otherwise below 23 − random(5), double. Before the start of the game ([0xdd6ec8] after today, 0x456740): 0. The recovery (0x62bd10) with the condition and the rate. With the knock (−0x11) and the match knock list (+0x28): each knock of the person (type 7 only with player sheet +0xf of 15 or more) has the severity by +5 (above 95: 2; above 66: 1; above 51: 0; otherwise the previous knock's) and the injury type (0x62d140); a valid type: end of the current injury (0x62e700) and the new injury (0x62d250 with the game, or 0 for game −2).

Returns the match knock list (+0x28) item with the person's id, or 0. \n `Injury::find_match_injury(person)`: the item of the match knock list (+0x28; cursor +0xa restarts from +2, 0x68d1b0) with the person's id, or 0 (also with no list). Used by the staff screens (0x870650, 0x885820).

Ends the person's current injury: the history (except holidays), the return news at a human club (when asked), entry type 0xff and the record's +0xe set to −1. \n `Injury::end_player_injury(person, news)`, from the day's fitness (0x62c680, with news), from the match knocks (0x62c080, without) and from the fitness restart (0x62bfa0, without): with a current injury (+0xe of the record, index into the 0x30-byte table at [this+4]; −1 none): except holidays (type 0x51), the history ([this+0xc], 0x58e340 with +0x14 and +0x18 of the record); with `news` and the person's club (+0x39) human (0x600a50), the return news (0x630ee0 with 1 and the type). The type becomes 0xff and +0xe −1. Without a person: the error box (line 0xc87).

Stores an illness outbreak (date, type, club, fixture) if it takes hold (type 4 never; type 3 with 1 in 15, the others with 3 in 4; outside national teams) and re-sorts the array by date. \n `Injury::add_illness_outbreak(date, type, club, match)`: the type is the low byte; if the outbreak takes hold (`outbreak_takes_hold`), the vector grows by 30 when full (0x945667, or 0x944e46 with no vector; out of memory, the "Error" box for line 0xd01 and nothing), the outbreak is written at the end (date through 0x417c10) and the vector is re-sorted by date (qsort 0x945333 with 0x778e90).

Spreads the illness outbreaks up to the first one after today: one older than five days is removed; the others make random squad players of the club ill. \n `Injury::spread_illness_outbreaks()`; SEH frame without destructor. It walks the outbreaks (sorted by date) up to the first one after today. One older than five days (0x54c8e0) is marked to leave; the others spread: type 3 only on the day itself, with 1 to 4 ill (random of 4, +1); the others 0 to 2 (random of 3). Outside national teams (0x53b900), up to 20 tries: one of the 50 squad slots (random of 50, +0xd7), a player (id below [0xae2364]) without that illness (+0x1d of the 31-byte record at [this]) becomes ill (0x62d250: the type in the low byte of the outbreak's offset dword, as in the original; the outbreak's fixture). At the end, those leaving go from the front of the vector (the others move down) and the count drops.

Tells whether the person is in the close season: 1 without a person; 1 when the club (without the +0x1db mark) is out of its nation's season with less than 40 days to go and there is no future national call-up; otherwise 0. \n `injury_player_in_close_season(person)` (stdcall, ret 4; SEH frame without destructor): without a person, 1. With a national team (+0x24), its date (0x76e040 on [0xb74318], the national team's nation +0x53, the class from 0x76d780 by bit 3 of +0x5e) after today counts as called up. Without a club (+0x39), called up, or a club with +0x1db ≠ −1: 0. Otherwise, out of the season of the club's nation (0x669bd0 with the two dates) and with less than 40 days to go (0x54cdb0 from today to the second date, 16 bits unsigned): 1; otherwise 0.

Sets each squad player's initial fitness from the club's pre-season days; non-players leave the squad slot. \n `Injury::init_squad_fitness()`; SEH frame without destructor. For each club (except national teams), the pre-season days (`preseason_days`; 0 in season, up to 40); each of the 50 slots (+0xd7) with a person whose id is below [0xae2364]: a player (+0x61): v = days − (player's +0x34, natural fitness)/2 − (person's +0x5b)/4 (signed, truncated), between 1 and 40, and the fitness (+8 of the 31-byte record at [this]) = 10000 − 75 × v; anyone who is not a player leaves the slot (0), and if their club (+0x39) is this one: job (+0x3d) 0xb becomes clubless and 8, 0xf becomes 8, 0xd becomes 6.

Allocates every person's 31-byte injury record fully fit; players may get a recurring injury (1 in 10) or start injured (1 in 100); the totals go to 0xde1f64. \n `Injury::init_records()`: [this] = 31 bytes per person of [0xae2364] (0x944e46; out of memory, the "Error" box for line 0x7d0 and nothing). Each record: today's date (0x417c10), form and condition 10000 (+8, +0xa), wear 0 (+0xc), no injury (+0xe −1), no recurring injury (+0x12 0xff), history −1 (+0x14, +0x18), +0x1d 0xff, +0x1e 50. A player (+0x61): the type drawn from 82 with weight (+8 of the 13-byte table at 0x9e7ad8) and 1 in 10 becomes recurring; 1 in 100 starts injured: category drawn from 12, type through 0x62d140 (severity −1) and the new injury 0x62d250. At the end the two totals in 0xde1f64 ("%d players with ...").

Clears the last entry of the person's injury history (+0x18 of the 31-byte record = −1, through 0x58f110). \n `Injury::reset_player_history(person)`: the person's injury history (31-byte record of the id at [this]) loses its last entry (0x58f110 on [this+0xc]: +0x18 = −1). Returns what 0x58f110 returns. Null person: as in the original (fatal box).

Resets a person's injury state: removes their items from the match knock list, ends the injury, rewinds the history and restarts the 31-byte record; bit 0 of +0xc of the 79-byte record is cleared. \n `Injury::reset_player(id)`: removes from list [this+0x28] (from the start: cursor +0xa back to +2) each item with the id (0x68d1f0); with an injury (+0xe ≠ −1), ends it (0x62e700, no news); restarts the history (0x631f90); the 31-byte record restarts: today's date (0x417c10 of [0xae2c90]), condition and form 10000 (+8, +0xa), wear 0 (+0xc), no injury (+0xe −1), no recurring injury (+0x12 0xff), history −1 (+0x14, +0x18), +0x1d 0xff. Bit 0 of +0xc of the 79-byte record ([0xae2d0c]) is cleared. Returns the address of that byte.

Applies a recovery day to person `p`'s 31-byte record (below −1000 in x87 with −0.0035 and 2.5; otherwise the rate or a random draw). \n In the 31-byte record (from [this]): +0xa receives `mark`; the word +0xc, below −1000, rises by trunc((v × −0.0035 − 2.5) × `rate`); otherwise, below 1200 − (player sheet +0x44 + player sheet +0x3c + person +0x5b, 16 bits), it rises by `rate`; otherwise, below 1250, it rises by random(`rate`) + 1. Null person or id outside [0xae2364]: nothing.

Returns the player's condition: fitness × match condition / 10,000 (minimum 100, maximum 9000 while recovering), or as a percentage (maximum 100). \n `Injury::get_condition(player, as_percent)`: the player's condition: form (+0xa) × match condition (+8) / 10,000 from the id's 31-byte record [this], at least 100 and at most 9000 while he is recovering (0x62c400 = 1); as a percentage (× 0x96bac8 + 0x968968, _ftol), at most 100. A person outside the players ([0xae2364]): 100 or 10,000. Null player: 0.

Updates the day's fitness (0x62c680) and returns the match condition (out of 10000, or as a percentage). \n `Injury::get_match_condition(player, as_percent)`: without a player, 0; an id outside the persons ([0xae2364]): 10000 (100 as a percentage); otherwise it updates the day's fitness (0x62c680, once a day) and returns the condition (31-byte record at [this], +0xa), as a percentage × 0.01f truncated. Only ax is the return value.

Updates a person's fitness once a day: the days since the last update become free, recovery, stopped (injury) or holiday days, which raise or lower fitness (+8) and match condition (+0xa); stores today's date. \n `Injury::update_player_fitness(person)`; SEH frame only for the local statics. Once a day (if date +0 of the person's 31-byte record at [this] is already today: nothing), called from the match condition (0x62c510), the injury state (0x62c400), the injuries day (0x62b7b0) and the return news (0x62e010): every person who plays, every day someone asks. T = days since the last update (0x54cc30). Injured (+0xe in the 0x30-byte table at [this+4]): by the days since the start (+0x20) against +0x2a and +0x28, the stopped days (loss), recovery days or free days, with the end of the injury (0x62e700) when it passes +0x28. Not injured: free days, except with the national team with a future date (0x76d780/0x76e040) or at a club out of season (0x669bd0, cached in 0xb63d2c/0xb63d30 with the dates 0xb63d18/0xb63d20): holidays (byte +0xa of the 79-byte record rises when random(+0x5b / 3 + 2) is zero, up to 50) and the pre-season return (15 days, or the middle of a random(2) with form × condition below 80%). The fitness (+8): recovery of 1000 − 12 × (+0x1e − natural (+0x34 of the player sheet), 0..100) per free day, loss of 66 per stopped day, capped by natural fitness, stretches above 7000/9000/9850 shrunk (0x96af30, 0x96bad0, 0x968968, 0x968918, 0x967880), and −55 per holiday day; the match condition (+0xa) rises 500 × free days and 250 × recovery days times the tiredness factor (+0xc). \n Writes both and today's date.

Applies the day's wear to word +0xc of person `id`'s 31-byte record (age, draws of 25 and 13, goalkeeper cap). \n From [this]: below −1000 it goes down 1; under 19 years old (+0x18 of the person in [0xae23bc]) and negative, it is zeroed; otherwise, from −500 up and with age ≥ random(25), it goes down 13, and in the other cases it goes down random(13); a goalkeeper (player sheet position +0xf = 20) stays up to 1050. Id outside [0xae2364]: nothing.

Compares the key date with that of a 0x16-byte return to training queue entry, for bsearch. \n `injury_compare_entry_dates(key, item)` (cdecl), the bsearch (0x946464) order of the return to training queue (0x16-byte entries) in Injury::post_due_recovery_news (0x62e010, every day): the date at +8 of the key before the item's (0x456770), −1; after (0x456740), 1; equal, 0.

Returns the player's recurring injury type, or 0xff when he has none or is not a player. \n `Injury::get_recurring_injury_type(person)`, from the news (0x77bc80), the physio's assessment (0x7a2650) and the screens: the type of the recurring injury (+0x12 of the person's 31-byte fitness record, at [this]); null person, id from [0xae2364] on, or no player sheet (+0x61): 0xff. The callers only read al.

Marks read the first unread news item with the id in the human's ring, unless it needs a reply, takes it off the count and, when asked, repeats it for the humans on the same network machine. \n `News::mark_item_read(manager, id, sync)`: in the human's ring of 100 slots (News +8, by id − [0xae2364] + 16), the first slot with the `id` not yet read (+0xda = 0) whose button (0x782b70 on 0xde1f64) does not ask for a reply (2) becomes read and leaves the count (+8 of the entry). No ring: 0. Otherwise (even when not found), with `sync`, it repeats (without sync) for the other humans (+0x5f = 1) on the same network machine (0x7fffa0) as the current human; returns 1. No manager, no id, or a manager of the machine: the "Error" box and 0.

Copies the news item with the id to the output: from the human manager's 100-slot ring or, without a manager, from all slots. \n `News::find_item_by_id(manager, id, out)`: copies (0x786010) into `out` the news item with the `id`: with a manager, among the 100 slots of his ring (no ring: 0); without a manager, among all slots (News +4). Found: 1; otherwise 0. No id, no output, or a manager of the machine: the "Error" box and 0.

Delivers the news item by scope: 0 the club manager, 1 the division's managers, 2 the country's, 3 the continent's, 4 all, 5 the competition region's; anything else shows the "Error" box. \n `News::send_by_scope(news, club, competition, nation, continent, scope)`: the scope (char) picks the delivery: 0 the club's manager (0x7861e0), 1 those of the division (0x7862d0, by the competition), 2 those of the country (0x7863f0, by the nation), 3 those of the continent (0x786640), 4 all (0x786780), 5 those of the competition's region (0x786860). Anything else: the "Error" box and 0. Returns what the delivery returns.

Applies the automatic reply for the club to the human's inbox, from the newest item to the oldest, up to the empty slot. \n `News::auto_respond_all(manager, club)`: from the newest to the oldest news item of the human's ring, up to the first empty slot (+0xd6 = 0), gives the automatic reply (0x784100) for the `club`. No manager or a manager of the machine: the "Error" box and 0; no ring or at the end: 1. TapeCall when going on holiday, when sacked and when hired.

Without "urgent only", tells whether there is an unread item; with it, whether an item needs a reply or is important and unread. \n `News::has_urgent_items(manager, urgent_only)`: without `urgent_only`, whether there is an unread news item (0x786fe0 > 0). With it, from the newest to the oldest of the human's ring, up to the first empty slot: 1 if one needs a reply (the text 0x782b70 on 0xde1f64 returns 2) or is important (+4 = 1) and unread (+0xda = 0). A manager of the machine: the "Error" box and 0.

Copies the text into the news item's slots from the given slot and returns the first free slot after it (at most 50). \n `NewsItem::set_slot_string(slot, text, next)`: copies the `text` into the news item's slots from `slot` (strncpy 0x9466d0 at +5 + 4·slot, up to 200 − 4·slot bytes), terminates the area (+0xcc = 0) and, with `next`, writes the first free slot after the text (the length with the terminating zero rounded up to 4, in slots, plus `slot`; at most 50). Slot outside 0..49 or no text: the "Error" box and 0; otherwise 1.

Sets the continent scope (+0xde = 3) and delivers the news to every active human manager whose club or nation is in the continent. \n `News::send_to_continent_managers(news, continent)`: continent scope (+0xde = 3) and delivery (0x785d40 with 0) to each active human manager whose club (+0x39) has its nation (+0x53) in the `continent` (+0x71) or whose nation (+0x1a) is in it. Returns 1, or 0 on the first refusal. Null news or continent: as in the original ("Error" box).

Delivers the news to the managers of the competition's nation (0x786520), else of its continent (0x786640), else to all (0x786780). \n `News::send_to_comp_region(news, comp)`: with the competition's nation (+0x5d), to the nation's managers (0x786520); otherwise, with the continent (+0x59), to the continent's (0x786640); otherwise to all (0x786780). Returns what the delivery returns. Null news or competition: as in the original ("Error" box).

Tells whether the news item is important for the person, by category and type (bids on the person's club, the humans...). \n `NewsItem::is_important_for(person)`: is the news important for the person (the byte +4 that the delivery 0x785d40 writes)? By the category (0x785670) and the type (+0): category 2, types 7 to 0xb, 0x27 and 0x28; category 4, 0xbb8, 0xbb9 and 0xbc4; category 5, a fixed list, 0xfa1 if the person is the manager of the club in data 5 (+0x19) and 0xfb6 if he is that of data 4 (+0x15) or of data 5; category 6, 0x1770 if data 0 (+5) is one of the 16 human managers; category 1, 0x1388; the rest, 0. The original calls 0x785670 up to six times (it only reads): the port calls it once. Null person or type outside 1..0x1790 (0x785670's box): as in the original.

Copies the text stored from the slot (+5 + 4 × slot) into the buffer (strncpy) and clears the last byte; returns 1. \n `NewsItem::get_slot_string(slot, dest, n)`: copies the text stored from slot `slot` (+5 + 4 × slot) into `dest` like strncpy (0x9466d0: up to the zero, padding with zeros up to `n`) and zeroes the last byte (`dest[n − 1]`). Returns 1. Slot outside 0..49, null destination or `n` < 1: as in the original ("Error" box and 0).

Sets the division scope (+0xde = 1) and delivers the news to every active human manager with a club in the division (+0x57); returns 1, or 0 on the first refusal. \n `News::send_to_division_managers(news, division)`: division scope (+0xde = 1) and delivery to each active human manager with a club (+0x39) in the `division` (+0x57). Returns 1, or 0 on the first refusal. Null news or division: as in the original ("Error" box).

Sets the nation scope (+0xde = 2) and delivers the news to every active human manager whose club or national team belongs to the nation (+0x53); returns 0. \n `News::send_to_nation_managers(news, nation)`: nation scope (+0xde = 2) and delivery to each active human manager whose club (+0x39) or national team (+0x24) belongs to the `nation` (+0x53). Returns 0. Null news or nation: as in the original ("Error" box).

Sets the nation scope (+0xde = 2) and delivers the news (0x785d40) to every active human manager with a club of the nation; the first refusal stops. \n `News::send_to_nation_club_managers(news, nation)`: the news gets the nation scope (+0xde = 2) and goes (0x785d40 with 0) to each of the 16 human managers (the last 16 of [0xae23bc], 0x6e bytes) who are active (+0x5f = 1) with a club (+0x39) of the `nation` (+0x53); the first refused delivery (0) stops it. Returns 0. Null news or nation: as in the original ("Error" box).

Counts the unread news in a human manager's inbox, in total or for one category. \n Without a category (0): the entry's total (+8, negative becomes 0). With a category: of the 100 news items in the inbox (start at entry +0; −1 = empty, 0), the occupied ones (+0xd6) of the category (0x785670) not yet read (+0xda = 0). Null manager or out of range: as in the original (error box).

Writes a value into a slot of a news item in the human manager's inbox and into its local copy. \n Writes `value` into slot `slot` (dword +5 + 4 × slot) of news item `id` (+0xd6) in the human manager's inbox, first into the `copy` (if any) and then into the inbox one; 1 if found. Empty inbox: only the copy, 0. Error cases: as in the original.

Gives the default replies for the manager's club and national team (0x7874b0) and empties his inbox (the 100 news items with +0xd6 = 0 and +0xda = 1). \n `News::clear_inbox(manager)`, from 0x6b28b0 and from loading the game (0x82a9c0): the default replies to the news of the manager's club (+0x39) and national team (+0x24) (0x7874b0); then the human's inbox (12-byte record at [this+8], by id − [0xae2364] + 16): +4 = +0 and +8 = 0; with the first news item (+0, −1 none), the 100 news items of 0xdf bytes from it ([this]) with +0xd6 = 0 and +0xda = 1. No manager or a negative index: the error box (lines 0x24c1 and 0x24cc).

Returns a new array with the human's inbox items, newest first, only those of one category when asked, and the count. \n `News::get_inbox_items(manager, count, category)`: a new vector of 100 news items (malloc 0x944e46 of 0x571c, on the first one found; `*count` = 0) with the news of the human's ring, from the newest to the oldest up to the empty slot, only those of the `category` (0x785670) if it is not 0, copied (0x786010); `*count` adds one per news item. Returns the vector (0 if none; `*count` untouched). No manager or a manager of the machine: the "Error" box and 0.

Returns the news category by the thousands range of its type. \n (thiscall) The news category by the thousands of the type (+0): 1..999 → 2, 1000.. → 7, 2000.. → 3, 3000.. → 4, 4000.. → 5, 5000.. → 1, 6000..0x1790 → 6. Anything else: as in the original (error box). Returns the whole eax like the original (the type with al replaced).

Copies a news item (0xdf bytes): +0, +4, the 50 tokens (+5), the date (+0xcd), +0xd5, +0xd6, +0xda and +0xde. \n `NewsItem::operator=`: copies the news item (0xdf bytes) from `source`: +0 (dword), +4 (byte), the 50 tokens from +5 (dwords, in order), the date at +0xcd, +0xd5 (byte), +0xd6 and +0xda (dwords) and +0xde (byte). Returns `this`.

Sets up the referees on a new game: reviews them, sorts them by nation and quality, keeps 6 per nation (61 in some nations), builds the per-nation blocks with one slot per league, draws the missing referees and shares the nation's referees among the slots. \n `OfficialsManager::set_up_officials()`, from the constructor (0x79b580) on a new game. It reviews the records (0x79caa0), sorts them by nation and quality (qsort 0x79d4e0) and, per nation, keeps the first 6 (nation with +0x11c zero) or 61 (the first of each nation after the first one is not kept: the count restarts on it), copied (0x79c530) into a new table; the per-nation blocks (this+0xc, 0x102 bytes: +0 the nation, +4 the referees, +8 the first, +0xc the demand, +0x10 the competitions and 15 slots of 16 bytes at +0x12): each league (0x4b0700, not a friendly 0x5c6710, with nation +0x5d) gets a slot with the demand (+0x3e of the competition) / 2 + 10; a nation with competitions asks for the largest × the number and, if short, draws the missing ones (0x79c5c0); without competitions and with fewer than 5, it draws up to the nation's +0x8e (1..5). The indexes (+0), the first of each nation and, per nation, the slots sorted (qsort 0x79d410) with each one's share; this+4 the count and this+8 the flags (calloc).

Orders a nation's referee slots by competition level (the invalid ones last or first), tie by id. \n `officials_manager_compare_comp_level(a, b)` (cdecl), the order of a nation's competition slots (qsort of 0x79bf60, 16-byte entries with the competition at +0xc): `a`'s competition outside 0..[0xae2378]: 1; `b`'s outside: −1; by level (+0x69, word, of the 0x6b-byte competition in [0xae23d0]); same level: the difference of the ids.

Orders the referees by nation and, within it, by quality (+0x28 × 50 + +0x22) from highest to lowest; tie by index, descending. \n `officials_manager_compare_nation_then_quality_desc(a, b)` (cdecl), the qsort order of 0x79bf60 (those kept per nation): by nation (id) and, within it, by quality from highest to lowest; tie: `b`'s index +0 minus `a`'s.

Orders the referees by nation and by quality from lowest to highest; tie by index, ascending. \n `officials_manager_compare_nation_then_quality_asc(a, b)` (cdecl), the qsort order of 0x79c5c0 (after the new referees): by nation and by quality from lowest to highest; tie: `a`'s index +0 minus `b`'s.

Chooses a match referee: the referee range for the competition, a random one in it and the next free one. \n `OfficialsManager::choose_match_official(match, out)`, from setting up the day (0x6b3c10, output at +0x2e of the match). Removed match (−2): 0 (eax 0xffffff00, as in the original). The referee range: without a competition, the home club's nation (+0x1c, +0x53) or a random one; a friendly (0x5c6710 on [0xae2c74]), the home club's; a competition without an object ([0xadadfc]), as without a competition; a competition of types 2 and 4 (+0x42), the top quarter (ftol of 0.75 and 0.25 of the count) of the first nation, starting from a random one, of the continent (+0x59 of the competition, or +0x71 of the home club's nation, of the away club's, or a random one) that is not that of either club (a neutral nation); in the others, the competition's range in its nation's block (+0x5d; or the home club's, the away club's, or a random one), the last that matches, or the whole block. Count 1: the first; otherwise first + random(count − 1). Busy (the byte of the referee's id in [this+8]): the next in the range, wrapping around; all busy, the drawn one. Writes the index (word) and returns 1 in al (the rest of eax with the index, as in the original).

Clears the daily referee busy bytes. \n `OfficialsManager::clear_busy_flags`, in the day loop (0x5cccd0) and in the run up to the start date (0x5cc850): zeroes the [this+4] busy bytes at [this+8] (the count and the vector re-read at each step). Returns the count (0 if not positive), like the original's eax.

At each league's season start, replaces the referees of its range over 45 (or over 40, one in three) with new random ones and clears the range's statistics rows. \n `OfficialsManager::renew_officials(comp)`, at the start of each league's season (83 callers). Without a competition, without an object ([0xadadfc]), of types 4 and 2 (+0x42), or without a count (0x4b0700): 0. The competition's range in its nation's block (+0x5d, or a random one), the first that matches, or the whole block. Each referee of the range (0x2b-byte records in [0xae23e8]; null record: the "Error" box): over 45 years old (the year as a byte, minus 1 before his birthday), or over 40 and random(3) zero, becomes another: two names from his nation (0x539c60, +4 and +8), +0x25 random(16) + 5 (or, with random(10) zero, random(11) + random(11)), the year (+0xe) game year − 27 + random(5) and the day (+0xc) random(340). Then it zeroes the statistics rows (17 bytes at [this]) of each referee of the range (+4, +8, +0xa, +0xc, +0xf; the `add eax, 0x11` at 0x79d149 stays inside the loop). Returns 1 (only al counts).

Reallocates the referee table, generates `count` new referees of the nation and sorts the table by nation and quality. \n `officials_manager_add_random_officials(count, nation)` (thiscall with this unused, ret 8), from setting up the referees of a new game (0x79bf60, in nations with few referees). A nation without a continent (+0x71): nothing. It reallocates the table ([0xae23e8], 0x945667) to [0xae2390] + count records (out of memory: error and the game stops), generates `count` new records at the end (generate_official: names by weight, random ratings and attributes, born in the 1960s), adds the count to [0xae2390] and sorts the whole table (qsort 0x945333 with 0x79d480: nation, +0x28 × 50 + +0x22, id).

Repairs each referee record: the nation from the names, out-of-range ratings and attributes drawn again, and a too-old birth date. \n `officials_manager_validate_officials()` (cdecl), at the start of setting up the referees of a new game (0x79bf60). For each of the [0xae2390] records (0x2b bytes in [0xae23e8]): without a nation (+0x16), the one from the nation table by the index (+0x37) of the first name (+4), of the second (+8), or a random one; the words +0x22, +0x1e and +0x20 outside 1..200: random(80) + 1 plus the nation's byte +0x8e (+0x22) or 4 times it (+0x1e, +0x20; the redone +0x20 is at least +0x1e); the bytes +0x24..+0x2a outside 1..20 drawn by the bands of +0x1e (above 120, above 80); born before the date 0x549f70(1, 1, 1910, −1) (year unsigned, then the day signed), year 1960 + random(10) and day random(300) + 1.

Copies a 0x2b-byte referee record field by field, the date through the date copy. \n `Official::operator=(src)`, from setting up the referees of a new game (0x79bf60, the records that are kept). Copies the 0x2b-byte record field by field (+0, +4, +8; the date at +0xc through 0x417c10; +0x14, +0x16, +0x1a, +0x1e, +0x20, +0x22, the bytes +0x24..+0x2a). Returns `this`.

Writes the referees and their statistics into the off.dat item of the save. \n `OfficialsManager::save_official_stats(save)`: writes into the `off.dat` item the number of referees [0xae2390], the 0x11-byte records from [+0] (one per referee), the number of nations [0xae2350], the 0x102-byte records from [+0xc] (one per nation) and one byte per referee from [+8]; returns 1 (in the low byte). No container or an error on opening: the "Error" box (officials_manager.cpp 0x142, 0x14a) and 0; no referees or an error on writing: the box (0x150, 0x156, 0x15c, 0x164, 0x16c, 0x174), it closes the item and 0.

Rebuilds a retired person from the regen queue as a young player: player record, nation, names, languages, age and ability, reputations, birth date, personality attributes and, by chance, a club. \n `PLAYER_REGEN::regenerate_as_youth_player(person)`, from the regen queue (0x7a65d0) for every young regen. A person not retired (bits 0x30 of +0xb of the 79-byte record) or with a club: it only clears the bits. Otherwise: leaves the national team (0x775ba0), takes the front record of the player record pool (this+0x3c, 16-byte entries: record, nation, second nation; 0x7a8470), becomes a player (+0x5f = 2, +0x61 the record) and the 79-byte record gets the regen mark (0x40) and loses the others; the person's lists and histories are cleared (fog, statistics, history, suspensions, injuries, dispute, discipline, fitness, contracts); the record's nation (or, if its reputation is below 100, with 1/4, any one with reputation below 100), the second nation (Spain with 1/100 keeps the previous one; another one other than the Basque Country with 2/3 none), the nation's names, the languages (all removed; the nation's by weight, level (weight − (20 − +0x56) × 10) / 75 up to 10), the joining date today, +0x3d/+0x28 = 11. The age and ability: a small nation (reputation below 350, +0x11c zero) by the reputation (23..27 or 17..23 years) and by the PA; otherwise by the record's position and the age by random(10000) (15..18 rare, 16..18, 17..20, 21..26). The reputations (+9, +0xb, +0xd), the ability caps, the birth year and day, the age (0x53ab90), the personality attributes (+0x1b, +0x36, +0x1d, +0x2e, +0x34, +0x44, +0x3c, +0x3d, +0x1e, +0x24, +0x2c, +0x2f, +0x21) by age; under 19 and a nation with +0x11c, with 3/4, the best club (0x7ad0e0) and the contract (0x7a6f10, news 0x7a8ba0 at a human club and the assistant manager may like him); otherwise, by chance, a club of the nation (0x7ad590). Without a club and under 20, the reputations up to 1250 and +0xd = 1. At the end, the attributes normalised (0x538ec0, 0x538bc0).

Finds the person of a player_setup.cfg line by the three names: among all persons or, with the club name, in its squad (when asked) and its manager. \n `player_setup_find_staff(first, common, second, club, in_squad)` (cdecl). Without `club` (null or empty): the first of the [0xae2364] persons ([0xae23bc], 0x6e bytes) whose non-empty names match (each name checked only if both the text and the person's name exist). With `club`: the club with that name (0x545880, 51 characters); not found, 0. With `in_squad` 1: the first of the 50 squad slots (+0xd7) whose names match; otherwise (or none in the squad), the club's manager (+0xcf) if the names match; otherwise 0.

Copies the next quoted text of the line (skipping spaces and line breaks before it) and returns where to continue. \n `player_setup_read_quoted_token(source, dest)` (cdecl): copies into `dest` the text between the first quotes of `source`: spaces and '\r' at the start of the text and '\n' before it are skipped; it ends at the closing quote or at the zero (the destination gets the zero) and returns the pointer two past the end.

Returns the type bit of a player_setup.cfg line. \n `player_setup_type_from_name(name)` (cdecl): the bit of the line type (INJURY 1, MANAGER_CONF 2, RETIREMENT 0x200, INT_RETIREMENT 4, FUTURE_TRANSFER 8, LOAN 0x10, NANDROLONE and DRUGS 0x100, MISCONDUCT 0x1000, FALSE_PASSPORT 0x800, ARSE 0x20, PRESET_TACTICS 0x2000, COLOURBLIND 0x400, GERMAN 0x80, AWOL 0x40; none 0), used when applying the lines (0x7a3a10) on game creation.

Processes the day's pending retirements: drops some, retires the others (news, contract, national team, squad), possibly turns the player into a coach, stores the record in the regen pool or queues the regen slot, and announces the future ones. \n `PLAYER_REGEN::process_retirements()`, every day from the day loop; SEH frame with no destructor on the normal path. The local slot for the regen (id and the default date 0x54a110, which leaves leap flag 1 in it); it sorts the pending retirements ([this+4], [this+8] of 26 bytes: +0 the person, +4 the club or −1, +8/+0xa the announcement day and year, +0x10/+0x12 those of the retirement, +0x18 the reason, +0x19 announced) with 0x7ae2a0 and walks through them (the pointer only advances on an announcement: 0x7a8690 pulls the following ones). Due (the date has passed): a young player (up to 29) with a club or flag, except reason 8, gives up; with a contract record (0x4cf6d0) or under offer (0x8cde70), gives up (flags & 0xcf); one who moved club less than 210 days ago, up to 37 years old, with a contract, off the list and without +0x45, stays; otherwise the news (0x7a92e0), the offers (0x4ccbf0), the contract, the national team (0x775ba0), the watch lists, the squad (0x7aace0), the absences (0x4196a0, 0x4197c0) and the dispute (0x56a090); the player may become a coach (attributes from reputation and record); with a player record and a non-player record, the record goes to the pool (0x7a8350) and the new contract (0x85e960); otherwise the regen slot (0x7a87d0) and, with a non-player record, he leaves the jobs (0x7aaeb0) or is rebuilt as a non-player (0x7ab340). Not due: with the announcement date passed and not announced, the announcement news (0x7aa340, if flags & 0x30 are not 0x10), the announced flag and flags 0x10; otherwise it stops. At the end it sorts the regen slots ([this+0x10], [this+0x14] of 12 bytes) with 0x7ae240.

Posts news item 0xbba about the retirement to the managers (all, the country, the division, the club or the interested clubs, by fame) and pays the club insurance when injury retires a valuable player. \n `player_regen_post_retirement_news(person, reason, announced)` (stdcall, ret 0xc; 0x7a59e0 puts this in ecx, unused; SEH frame with no destructor on the normal path). No person, a player with job 8 or 5, no club, or a club without a human manager (0x7875e0): nothing. News 0xbba (local): 0..3 the person (id and the +0x33 of +4/+8/+0xc), 4 the reason, 5 announced, 6 the club (−1 if none), 7 the nation (+0x1a) with the national team caps (+0x22) or −1, 8 the job (0xf becomes 8, 0xd becomes 6), 9 the reputation, 0xa +0x28, 0xb player record and non-player record, 0xc the age, 0xd the non-player record, 0xe the player record. The interested clubs (0x8d1da0 on [0xde1f54] with 0xa, up to 30, only for a player). A major nation (+0x85 above 8) and a star (+0xd of the player record above 8500, or a manager of job 5 with +0xc above 8750): to everyone (0x786780); a lesser star (+0xd above 7500, or job 5 with +0xa above 7250): to the managers of the nation and of the club's nation (0x7863f0); a manager of job 5 at a club with a division: to those of the division (0x7862d0); a non-player: to the club (0x7861e0); a player: to the interested clubs. Reason 8 (injury) with +0xb of the player record above 4250 and a contract club (0x4cf5a0, cached in [0xae1080]): the insurance (0x58a980 with +0x52).

Posts news item 0xbce about a youth player joining the club, with the assistant manager's or a coach's verdict on his ability. \n `player_regen_post_youth_promotion_news(player, club)` (stdcall, ret 8; SEH frame with no destructor on the normal path), from the young regen (0x7abac0). No player or club: nothing. News 0xbce (local): 0..3 the player (id and the +0x33 of +4/+8/+0xc), 4 the club id, 5 the age, 6 the club's strength (+0x7f) above 15. The assistant manager (+0xd3) and the five coaches (+0x19f) give their opinion until the first one who gives a verdict: the perceived reputation = random(2500) + club reputation (+0x80) / 2 + strength × 12.5 (truncated); the two perceived abilities (0x6e86d0 with 2 and with 1) against reputation / 50 + 75 (verdict 2) and reputation / 100 + 50 (1). With a verdict: 7 assistant?, 8..0xb who (id and names), 0xc and 0xd the verdicts; otherwise −1. Delivered at the club's scope (0x786090).

Signs the regen for a club: the first free squad slot, the value, the contract end, the contract and the default wage; returns 1 (0 without a slot). \n `player_regen_sign_for_club(person, club)` (stdcall, ret 8; SEH frame only for the local dates), from PLAYER_REGEN::regenerate_as_youth_player (0x7abac0) for every young regen: in the first free slot of the 50 in the squad (+0xd7; no slot, 0) the person, her club (+0x39) and +0x4e = 0; the value (+0x52) through 0x4d0c60 (club, 1, −1, 0), the squad (0x540980 with 1), one time in four (random(4) = 0) 0x547d90 (person, club, 0); a club with +0x64 = 3: value at most 5000. The contract end (+0x46): under 19 (+0x18), today's year + 2; otherwise + random(6) + 1; in the month of the club's season end (0x4d45f0) and on day random(28) + 1 (0x549f70). The contract (0x4c7950 with the value); a human club (0x600a50 with 1, 1): for the reserves (0x4cc0f0) and the contract bits +0x4f (0x60 high) and +0x35 (1 low). With a contract: the default wage (0x8626e0), +0x3a = 0 and, outside the human club, the end (+0x2f) at most today's year + 5 (with day +0x2d = 0). At the end the squad numbers ([0xdd7ef0], 0x85add0 and 0x85a470). Returns 1.

Replaces the person's pending retirement with a new one through injury (reason 8), random(days / 2) + 1 days ahead. \n `PLAYER_REGEN::schedule_injury_retirement(person, days)`, from the new injury (0x62d250) that ends the career; SEH frame only for the local dates. It removes the person's pending retirement (the first with her id in the 26-byte table [this+4], count +8; 0x7a8690) and adds (0x7a8510) the new one: id, club id (+0x39, or −1), today's date + random(days / 2) + 1 (0x54c5b0) at +8 and again at +0x10, reason 8 (+0x18) and 0 (+0x19).

Builds news 0xbbb (id, names, reason, contract club, age) and sends it to the managers of the interested clubs. \n `player_regen_post_retirement_announcement_news(person, reason)` (stdcall, ret 8; SEH frame without destructor), from PLAYER_REGEN::process_retirements (0x7a59e0): except for a player (+0x61) with job +0x3d 8 or 5, news 0xbbb in a local (0x77bbe0 with 0) with data 0 = id, 1 to 3 = the names (+0x33 of +4, +8 and +0xc), 4 = reason, 5 = the id of the contract club (0x4cf5a0, cached in [0xae1080]; club of the 0x245-byte record in [0xae23b4] by +4; a contract of type +0x35 & 0x3f = 5 or no club: −1) and 6 = the age (+0x18); it goes to the managers of up to 30 interested clubs ([0xde1f54], 0x8d1da0 with 10).

Appends to the pool of free player records the player record id of a person who stops playing, with the nation and second nation, growing the table by 250. \n `PLAYER_REGEN::add_player_data_to_pool(person, nation, second)`: appends to the free player pool (16 bytes at [this+0x3c], count +0x40, capacity +0x44) the player record id (+0x61) of the person with index `person` (0x6e-byte record in [0xae23bc]) at +0, the nation at +4 and the second nation at +8 (+0xc is left as it is). Count = capacity − 1: grows by 250 (realloc 0x945667; out of memory, box 0xa0a and end). From process_retirements (0x7a59e0), when a player who also has a non-player record stops playing.

At a new game, decides whether a person with a club retires this season: non-players by the job age limit, players by the profile limit, the ability, the club's competition and the contract status; fills the output and the dates. \n `player_regen_check_initial_retirement(person, out)` (thiscall without reading this, ret 8): on a new game (from 0x7a58f0), does the person with a club (+0x39) retire this season? The contract (contract_with_current_club) and the status (contract_status). Without a player record (+0x61): without a manager record (+0x69) always; with it, when past the limit (non_player_age_limit); reason 0x20. A player: past the record's limit (player_age_limit), v = ⌊⌊1 − (age − limit) × 0.1⌋ × ability (+0xb)⌋ (16 bits); over 45, reason 1. A club without a competition (+0x57; without a club, a nation without +0x11c): random(3) ≠ 0 retires, otherwise only a negative status with a club. Otherwise: v ≥ 5000 or +5 > 80, no; +5 < 10 or v < 1500, yes; with a club, only a negative status; without a club, reason 2 with random(25 × +0x3c) = 0. Whoever retires: the output (fill_retirement_entry: id, club, reason) and the announcement and retirement dates (set_retirement_dates, by the key nation; without a valid key nation, tomorrow); returns 1.

In the search for new retirements, decides whether the person retires: like the initial check, with the limit adjusted by contract and wage, unemployment, contract end and potential; without a key nation, dates drawn near today. \n `player_regen_check_retirement(person, out)` (thiscall without reading this, ret 8), from the search for new retirements (0x7a5790). Without a player record: as in 0x7a79c0 (reason 0x20). A player above the record's limit: over 33, the limit drops 1 without a contract with the club, or with +0x45 in the contract and +0x15/+0x14 of the record = 20, or the high nibble of +0x4f = 7; with a club and a contract with wage (+0xc) above 750 × (+0x59 + 10) until after this year (+0x2f), it drops 1 (and 1 more with +0x59 < 6). v = ⌊(1 − (age − limit) × 0.075) × ability (+0xb)⌋ (16 bits). Reason 1: over 45; over 34 without a club and unemployed for more than 65 days (since +0x3e); 3 years above the limit, over 31 and the contract's +0x3e > 5; 4 above: without a club; or a contract less than 300 days from its end (0x85fa00), status below 50 and manager (+0x69) or +0x57 > random(20) with potential × 0.85 above the current ability (+7 and +5). Then v > 5500, no. A club in a competition not running in the game ([[0xadadfc] + id × 4] = 0, or without +0x57; without a club, a nation without +0x11c): random(3) = 0 retires; with a club and a negative status too; otherwise only with v < 3500. Otherwise as in 0x7a79c0 (+5 > 100 no; +5 < 10 or v < 1500 yes; with a club only a negative status; without a club reason 2 with random(25 × +0x3c) = 0). Whoever retires: the output and the dates (without a valid key nation, set_dates_no_key_nation, near today); returns 1.

At a new game, tests every eligible person (0x7a79c0), adds those who retire to the list and sorts it. \n `PLAYER_REGEN::build_initial_retirement_list`; SEH only for the local dates, with an empty destructor. On a new game, each person (0x6e bytes in [0xae23bc], up to [0xae2364], re-read at each step) with id below [0xae2364] − 16, without bits 0x30 of +0xb of the 79-byte record ([0xae2d0c]) and without a contract (0x4cf5a0) with +0x49 is tested (0x7a79c0); whoever retires goes into the list (0x7a8510). At the end the qsort of the list ([this+4], count +8, 26 bytes, 0x7ae2a0).

Tests every eligible person for retirement by age (0x7a7310) or unemployment (0x7a8050), adds those who retire and sorts the list. \n `PLAYER_REGEN::find_new_retirements` (on the days of 0x5d6250); SEH only for the local dates, with an empty destructor. Each person (0x6e bytes in [0xae23bc], up to the end computed with the count [0xae2364] at the start). Excluded: under 30 years old (+0x18) at a club of a competition that runs in the game ([[0xadadfc] + id × 4] of the competition +0x57); id from [0xae2364] − 16 on (re-read at each step); bits 0x30 of +0xb of the 79-byte record ([0xae2d0c]); those already in the list ([this+4], 26 bytes, count +8); a contract (0x4cf5a0) with +0x49. The others: retirement by age (0x7a7310) or, failing that, the unemployed one (0x7a8050); whoever retires goes into the list (0x7a8510). At the end the qsort of the list (0x7ae2a0).

Scores a person as the donor of non-player data: −10000 when under 31 or flagged; otherwise random draws and attribute terms. \n `player_regen_score_non_player_candidate(person)` (stdcall, ret 4): the person's score as donor of the non-player data (from 0x7a6e60, for each non-player person). −10000 with +0x69, with bits 0x30 of +0xb of the 79-byte record ([0xae2d0c]) or under 31 (+0x18). Otherwise random 150 × (age − 31); with a club (+0x39) with reputation (+0x80) and a player record (+0x61), + 250 × (current ability +0xb ÷ reputation); with a player record, + random(⌊(+0x2f ÷ 2)³⌋) (pow 0x945ff0 and _ftol), +100 with +0xd > 7500 and +50 with +0xb > 7500; the attributes + 5 × (3 × (+0x5d + +0x5a) + 2 × (+0x59 + +0x58) + +0x56) + ⌊+0x5b²⌋ + ⌊+0x57²⌋. With a club: a random draw of the score (+75 if the club has no +0xcf); without a club: + (+0x22)², and the score doubles if the player's +0xd exceeds a random(10000) (it reads the player record without checking, as the original does). Hot (every person on each call): no counter.

qsort comparator of the retirement list: by the effective date, year and day; on a tie by id. \n `player_regen_compare_retirements(a, b)` (cdecl): the qsort of the retirement list (0x1a-byte records; from 0x7a59e0 every day, which stops at the first future entry, from the initial lists 0x7a5790/0x7a58f0 and from 0x7a8690): by the effective date (entry_effective_date: the announcement +8 if not yet past, otherwise the retirement +0x10), the year unsigned and the day signed; on a tie by the id (+0). Without `a`, −1; without `b`, 1. Hot (qsort): no counter.

qsort comparator of the regen queue: by year (+6), day (+4) and id (+0). \n `player_regen_compare_queue_entries(a, b)` (cdecl): the qsort of the regen queue (0xc-byte records, at the end of 0x7a59e0 every day; 0x7a65d0 creates the regens of the due entries): by year (+6, unsigned), then by day (+4, signed), then by id (+0). Without `a`, −1; without `b`, 1. Hot (qsort): no counter.

Removes the player from his club and national team and changes the player job to the staff job; without a kept job, clears the club and the national team. \n `PLAYER_REGEN::retire_from_playing_staff(p)` (stdcall, ret 4): removes `p` from the club (+0x39) and the national team (+0x24) (`remove_from_team`: the tactics and the 50 slots) and changes the player job to the staff one (tables 0x7aae60 and 0x7aae90): by the club job (+0x3d, signed byte; outside 0..16 the default applies) 12 → 5, 13 → 6, 15 → 8 (stays at the club), 0 and 16 (warning "already retired") nothing, 1 to 10 the routine ends there, the others 0x10 (retired). Then by the national team job (+0x28) in the same way, but 12/13/15 write into +0x3d (the original writes there, not into +0x28) and the default writes 0x10 into +0x28. With no job kept, the club (+0x39) and the national team (+0x24) are zeroed. No SEH, no random draw.

Picks the best-scored club (0x7ad220) among those where the youngster is not a foreigner, that are not a B team, that may approach him and with a squad under 50. \n `PLAYER_REGEN::pick_best_club_for_player(player)`: among the clubs ([0xae23b4], 0x245 bytes; the first [0xae235c] − 2 × [0xae2350], re-read on every loop) where the player is not a foreigner (0x53d980 with the nation +0x53 and 1), that are not the B team of a pair (0x540a50 with 1, finding the partner with 0), not vetoed (`is_basque_restricted`), that may approach him (0x8ce990) and with a squad (0x53c590) under 50, the one with the highest score (0x7ad220, random; compared in 16 bits, starting from −25000). None: 0. No SEH; the partner local is only read when 0x540a50 finds it (and writes it).

Picks, from the club list of the youngster's nation, the club with the highest random draw of the score by reputation against ability, among those that may approach him and with a squad under 50. \n `PLAYER_REGEN::pick_club_from_nation_list(player)`: walks the club list of the youngster's nation (`player_regen_youth_list_nation`, some nations mapped to [0x9cf2e4]; word +0 is the count, cursor +0xa restarts from +2, the iterator 0x68d1b0 returns the id) and, among the clubs not vetoed (`is_basque_restricted`), that may approach him (0x8ce990) and with a squad (0x53c590) under 50, keeps the one with the highest random draw of the score (5000 + reputation +0x80 minus its distances to the ability of the player record +0x61: +0xb, +7 × 50 and +5 × 50, in 16 bits), compared in 16 bits starting from −25000. No list or an empty list: 0. A list that ends before the count: the "Error" box (line 0x19e9) and 0. No SEH.

Appends (id, nation, second nation) to the 16-byte spare non-player record list (+0x1c); grows by 250 when the player pool (+0x40/+0x44) is full, as in the original. \n `PLAYER_REGEN::add_spare_non_player_record(id, nation, second)`: appends (id +0, nation +4, second nation +8) to the 16-byte list of spare non-player records ([this+0x1c], count +0x20, capacity +0x24; taken out by 0x7a82b0). The original decides to grow by the free player pool (count +0x40 = capacity +0x44 − 1), not by this list: kept faithfully. Grows by 250 (realloc 0x945667; out of memory, box 0x9c4 and end).

Appends the record fields to the 26-byte pending retirement table (+4), growing by 250. \n `PLAYER_REGEN::add_retirement(record)`: appends to the 26-byte table of pending retirements ([this+4], count +8, capacity +0xc) the record's fields +0, +4 (dwords), +0x18 (byte), +8, +0xa, +0x10, +0x12 (words) and +0x19 (byte), in that order (+0xc..+0x10 and +0x14..+0x18 are left as they are). Count = capacity − 1: grows by 250 (realloc 0x945667; out of memory, box 0xa53 and end).

Puts the person into the regen queue (+0x10) with the dates; the non-player data goes into the spare list (+0x1c, random nation if none) and the player data into the free pool (+0x3c). \n `PLAYER_REGEN::queue_staff_for_regen(entry)`: the person with id +0 of the entry (0x6e-byte record in [0xae23bc]) enters the regen queue (12 bytes at [this+0x10], count +0x14, capacity +0x18: id +0, words +4 and +6 of the entry). With non-player data (+0x69): in the 16-byte list [this+0x1c] (count +0x20, capacity +0x24) their id +0, the nation (+0x1a; without a nation, a random draw 0x90cfc0 among the [0xae2350]) +4 and the person's id +0xc. With player data (+0x61): in the free player pool [this+0x3c] (count +0x40, capacity +0x44) their id +0, the nation's +4 (without checking for null, as in the original) and the person's +0xc. Each list grows by 250 when count = capacity − 1 (realloc 0x945667; boxes 0xaac, 0xac5, 0xae9 and end; in the third the original checks the count, not the pointer: kept faithfully). Id outside 0..=[0xae2364]: as in the original (box 0xa9d).

Removes a pending retirement: finds it (26 bytes), pulls the next ones up (0x7a8780), blanks the last one (person −1) and lowers the count. \n `PLAYER_REGEN::remove_retirement(key)`: searches (bsearch 0x946464 with 0x7ae2a0) for the pending retirement in the vector ([this+4], [this+8] records of 26 bytes); found: pulls the following ones up one place (0x7a8780, the record copy), the last one gets person −1 and +0x18, +8, +0xa, +0x10, +0x12 zeroed, and the count goes down. Without re-sorting.

Decides whether an unemployed person retires: a weak manager without a club, a player unemployed for over a year, or anyone with no record; fills the entry (reason 0x10, the game date) and returns 1. \n `player_regen_check_unemployed_retirement(person, out)` (stdcall, ret 8): whoever is on the shortlist does not retire. With a manager record (+0x69): without a club (+0x39) and without +0x24, with +0xa of the record below 50 and random(5) = 0. Without it, with a player record (+0x61): off the list (checked again), without a club and without +0x24, unemployed for more than 365 days (365 × (year − year of +0x40) − day of +0x3e + day) and random(the player's rating +0xb) < 750. With neither record: always. Retires: the output (26 bytes) receives the person, reason 0x10, +0x19 = 0, the club (−1 if none) and the game date at +8 and +0x10; returns 1. Otherwise 0.

Picks the non-player with the highest positive score (0x7a7150) of the nation; with none, of any nation; otherwise 0. \n `player_regen_pick_staff_for_non_player_data(nation)`: among the non-player persons ([0xae23bc], 0x6e bytes, [0xae2364] − 16 of them, count re-read on every loop), the one with the highest positive score from 0x7a7150 (random; the incoming ecx goes along, as in the original) of nation `nation` ([+0x1a]+0 = nation; initial score −1000); with none, the one with the highest positive score of any nation (initial −15000); otherwise 0.

Returns the random score of how well the club suits the youth player: reputation against ability, youth facilities, human control and nation. \n The score of `club` for the young `player` (random(score)): 5000 + reputation (+0x80) minus its distances to the ability (player record +0x61: +0xb, and +7, +5 × 50); with +7 above random(20) + 100, the youth bonus (+0x7f, 20 = guaranteed, otherwise random(+0x7f) > random(20)); a club of an active competition (0xadadfc) with +7 > 50: the human club state (0xae2d14) and the reputation against the squad (`squad`); the youth coach (+0xcf → +0x69) of a computer club (0x600a50) or the human's bonus; the same nation (+0x1a/+0x53) and the Welsh clubs (Swansea, Cardiff, Wrexham) and Scotland. Only the low 16 bits of the score count.

Copies a pending retirement record: the person, the club, the two dates, the reason and the announced flag. \n Copies the pending retirement (0x1a bytes) from `source`: the person's id (+0) and the club's (+4), the dates at +8 and +0x10 (0x417c10, with the return value in a local), the reason (+0x18) and the announced flag (+0x19). Returns `this`.

Returns the injury type of a player_setup.cfg INJURY line by name (76 names, from cold to arthritis); none: 0x4b. \n `player_setup_injury_from_name(name)` (cdecl): the injury type (0..0x4c) by the name of the player_setup.cfg injury line (strncmp with the 76 names, each by its own length, in order; the first that matches); none: 0x4b. Used when applying the lines (0x7a3a10) on game creation. The return value counts through al (the original leaves the rest of eax from strncmp).

Builds one club list per nation; each club with a division joins its nation's list, except national teams and the clubs at 0x9d00a4/0x9d00a8. \n `PLAYER_REGEN::build_nation_club_lists()`; SEH frame for the `new`. [this] = 14 bytes per nation of [0xae2350] (0x944e46, no check), with a new list (0x944cf1 of 0xe and 0x68d020; out of memory, 0) per nation; each club of [0xae235c] goes (0x68d0d0, the 4 bytes of the id) into its nation's list (`injury_youth_list_nation`: clubs with a division, a nation with +0x11c only with +0x80 up to 2, except national teams and the clubs at 0x9d00a4/0x9d00a8).

Processes the regen queue every day: due youth regens are created, and with more than 2 spare coach records, count − 2 of them are given to persons who lend the data. \n `PLAYER_REGEN::process_regen_queue()`, from the day loop (0x5cccd0), every day. The youth regen queue ([+0x10], 12 bytes: +0 id, +4 date; count +0x14): from the front, while the first one's date is before today (0x456770) and +0x40 is not zero, the youth regen (0x7abac0) of the person (id outside 0..[0xae2364]: box "Invalid staff_id for regen" and end), the following ones move up one place (0x7a8b70) and the last gets id −1. Then, with more than 2 spare coach records ([+0x1c], count +0x20), for count − 2 of them: the person lending the data (0x7a6e60 by the first one's nation +4) gets the spare's non-player record (+0x69, [0xae23c0] + 0x44 × id); a former player: the swap of +0x10/+0x11 of the rating 20, the normalisation (0x539490), the job at the computer's club and the three ratings (+0xa, +8, +0xc) by the reputation, +9 and +0xd of the player record (band above 7500, or random(+0x57) and the other two; pow and bands); a non-player: random(1500) and random(500). The spare leaves (0x7a82b0).

Returns 1 when the person's id is on the retirement list, otherwise 0. \n `PLAYER_REGEN::is_retirement_pending(person)`: 1 when the person's id (+0) is on the retirement list ([this+4], 0x1a-byte records, count +8 signed), otherwise 0 (and 0 without a person). Used by MANAGER_MANAGER::is_staff_suitable_for_job 0x69fa4b: a non-player who is about to retire is not suitable as a manager.

Copies the first spare non-player record entry (id, nation, second nation) to the outputs and removes it from the list. \n `PLAYER_REGEN::take_spare_non_player_record(&id, &nation, &second)`, from contract_manager (0x4ce4e0, two calls): copies the first item of the spare non-player record pool (this +0x1c: id, nation and second nation) into the three outputs and removes it from the pool (PLAYER_REGEN::remove_spare_non_player_record 0x7a82b0 with the id read from the output); returns its eax.
